[^192]: Feast of Saint Spyridon Concluded (Violakis, pp. 250–251 § 4), Commemorations of Saint Eleutherios (Dec 15), the Prophet Daniel and the Three Holy Youths (Dec 17), and Forefeast of the Nativity with Saint Ignatius the God-bearer (Dec 20 § 1). Physical leaf p265 (printed page 250) and facing English leaf p266 (printed page 251) complete the Praises and Divine Liturgy of Saint Spyridon concurring with the Sunday of the Forefathers (§ 4), assigning 4 Beatitudes to the Tone and 4 to Ode 6 of the Forefathers' Canon, the Epistle of the Hierarch (2 Timothy 1:8–18) and the Gospel of the Forefathers (Luke 14:16–24). The Typikon then provides concise directives for three subsequent mid-December commemorations: (1) Saint Eleutherios, Hieromartyr Bishop of Illyricum (December 15), whose service on a weekday follows the Menaion, and on the Sunday of the Forefathers follows the exact template of Saint Spyridon (§§ 2–4); (2) The Holy Prophet Daniel and the Three Holy Youths Ananias, Azarias, and Misael (December 17), where the Typikon formulates a major liturgical principle: when December 17 coincides with the Sunday of the Forefathers, their independent Menaion service is completely omitted because Daniel and the Three Children are already explicitly numbered and commemorated within the primary Choir of the Forefathers celebrated on this Sunday; and (3) Saint Ignatius the God-bearer, Bishop of Antioch (December 20), which opens the five-day Forefeast period of the Nativity of Christ. On a weekday (§ 1), the Forefeast and the Saint's office are combined according to the Menaion. If December 20 falls on the Sunday before the Nativity, paragraph 2 begins detailing the transfer of the Saint's service to Saturday, December 19, breaking off mid-sentence at "transferred to the...", which resolves on physical leaf p267.

[^193]: Transfer of Saint Ignatius the God-bearer (December 20, §§ 2–3) and the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (The Holy Fathers, Case 1, § 1). Physical leaf p267 (printed page 252) and facing English leaf p268 (printed page 253) detail the rubrics when December 20 coincides with the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (the Sunday of the Holy Fathers). In this occurrence, the commemoration of Hieromartyr Ignatius is transferred and sung in advance on Saturday, December 19, combined with the commemoration of the Martyr Boniface of Tarsus. On Friday evening at Great Vespers (§ 2), 3 Prosomoia of Saint Ignatius and 3 of Saint Boniface are chanted at "Lord, I have cried", followed at "Glory" by *Θεοφόρε Ἰγνάτιε* ("God-bearing Ignatius") and at "Both now and ever" by *Ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν οὐρανῶν* ("The King of heaven"). Here Violakis inserts an important rubrical commentary in parenthetical text, observing that *Ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν οὐρανῶν* is the First Dogmatic Theotokion of Tone Plagal 4 (Tone 8) from Saturday Great Vespers, and highlighting the liturgical anomaly of why this specific Tone 8 Theotokion was prescribed in the Constantinopolitan tradition rather than the Theotokion of the Tone of the current week (as mandated by the General Rubrics in Protheoria § 8). On Saturday morning (§ 3), Matins and the Eucharistic Liturgy of the Saturday before Nativity are celebrated with the propers of Saint Ignatius and Saint Boniface (Galatians 3:8–12 and Luke 13:19–29). The text then introduces the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (the Sunday of the Holy Fathers, celebrated between December 18 and 24, focusing on the genealogy of Christ and the Old Testament righteous), articulating Case 1 (§ 1) for when this Sunday falls early on December 18 or 19. Leaf p268 concludes mid-sentence at "Glory"..., resolving on physical leaf p269.

[^194]: Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (The Holy Fathers, Case 1, §§ 2–3 concluded). Physical leaf p269 (printed page 254) and facing English leaf p270 (printed page 255) conclude Case 1 of the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (when occurring on December 18 or 19). At Saturday Great Vespers (§ 1 concl.), the Doxastikon at "Lord, I have cried" is the idiomelic hymn in Tone 6 *Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν* ("Daniel, a man of desires"), three Old Testament composite readings are read (Genesis 14:14–20, Melchizedek blessing Abram; Deuteronomy 1:8–11, 15–17, Moses appointing judges; and Deuteronomy 10:14–21, the majesty of God and circumcision of the heart), and the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 2 is *Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα* ("Great are the accomplishments of faith"). At Sunday Matins (§ 2), after the Polyeleos, the canon is the renowned Menaion composition *Κύματι θαλάσσης* ("By the wave of the sea"), borrowing the incipit and acrostic of the Great Saturday Canon. Violakis specifies a rare stichological directive: before the first Troparion following each Heirmos, the singers chant the Resurrection verse *Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ Ἀναστάσει σου, Κύριε* ("Glory to Thy holy Resurrection, O Lord"), while before all subsequent Troparia they chant the hagiographical verse *Ἅγιοι τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρεσβεύσατε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν* ("Saints of God, intercede for us"), concluding with "Glory" and "Both now and ever". After Ode 3, the Hypakoe is *Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον* ("An Angel cooled the furnace of the Children"); after Ode 6, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Fathers are sung; and at the Praises, 4 Resurrection Stichira are joined with 4 of the Fathers, concluding at "Glory" with *Τῶν νομικῶν διδαγμάτων ὁ σύλλογος* ("The assembly of legal teachings"). At the Divine Liturgy (§ 3), the Epistle is Hebrews 11:9–10, 32–40 (the cosmic catalogue of the faith of the Old Testament Saints, Abraham dwelling in tents, Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthae, David, Samuel, and the Prophets who through faith subdued kingdoms and stopped the mouths of lions) and the Gospel is Matthew 1:1–25 (the historical and theological Genealogy of Jesus Christ from Abraham through forty-two generations, culminating in the Virginal Conception and Birth of the Incarnate Word).


## Cohort 28 Footnotes

[^195]: Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (The Holy Fathers, Case 2: December 20–23). Physical leaf p271 (printed page 256) and facing English leaf p272 (printed page 257) set forth the liturgical rubrics when the Sunday before the Nativity of Christ occurs between December 20 and 23. In this occurrence, the dominical Resurrection office is combined with both the Fathers and the Forefeast of the Nativity (which commences on December 20). At Saturday Great Vespers (§ 4), at "Lord, I have cried", 4 Resurrection Stichira are joined with 3 Forefeast Prosomoia (*Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ* / "O all-blameless Virgin of God") and 3 of the Fathers (*Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοί* / "Today, ye faithful, let us celebrate the memory of the Fathers"), concluding at "Glory" with the Doxastikon in Tone 6 *Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν* ("Daniel, a man of desires") and at "Both now and ever" with the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; three Old Testament composite readings of the Fathers are read (Genesis 14:14–20; Deuteronomy 1:8–11, 15–17; Deuteronomy 10:14–21); at the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichira conclude at "Glory" with *Χαίρετε, προφῆται τίμιοι* ("Rejoice, ye honored Prophets") and at "Both now and ever" with the Forefeast Theotokion *Ἰδοὺ καιρὸς ἤγγικε* ("Behold, the time is at hand"); and the Dismissal Troparia combine the Resurrection, the Fathers (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), and the Forefeast (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*). At Sunday Matins (§ 5), after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon is followed at the Lite by "Glory": *Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες* ("Flashing like lightning bolts") and "Both now and ever": *Ἄκουε οὐρανέ* ("Hear, O heaven"); at the Kathismata following the Polyeleos, two Resurrection Kathismata are joined with one Forefeast Kathisma (*Τῶν προφητῶν αἱ ῥήσεις* / "The sayings of the Prophets") at the first stichologia, and two Resurrection with another Forefeast Kathisma (*Αὐλῶν ποιμενικῶν* / "While shepherds were piping") at the second stichologia; the Canon is the Menaion Canon of the Fathers (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*); after Ode 3, the Hypakoe *Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον* and Resurrection Kontakion are recited; after Ode 6, the Forefeast Kontakion *Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεέμ* ("Be glad, O Bethlehem") and Ikos *Τῆς σῆς, Παρθένε, κυήσεως* ("Of Thy conception, O Virgin") are chanted with the dual Synaxarion; and at the Praises, 4 Resurrection Stichira are combined with 4 of the Fathers. Leaf p272 concludes mid-sentence at § 6 ("After the Little Entrance,"), resolving on physical leaf p273.

[^196]: Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (Case 2 Concluded & Case 3: December 24 Eve Concurrence). Physical leaf p273 (printed page 258) and facing English leaf p274 (printed page 259) complete the Eucharistic Liturgy of Case 2 (§ 6), specifying the entrance Apolytikia (Resurrection, Forefeast, Fathers, Temple Patron), the Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον* ("Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"), and the appointed Epistle (Hebrews 11:9–10, 32–40) and Gospel (Matthew 1:1–25). The text then articulates Case 3 (§§ 7–8): when the Sunday before the Nativity falls on December 24 itself (the Paramony / Eve of the Nativity). Here Violakis formulates a crucial liturgical exception: because December 24 is the final and most intensive day of the Forefeast, the dominical Resurrection hymns are entirely suppressed at Saturday Great Vespers (§ 7), and the service is sung exclusively from the Menaion for the Fathers and the Forefeast. At "Lord, I have cried", 4 Prosomoia of the Fathers (*Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοί*) are combined with 4 of the Forefeast (*Προεορτάσωμεν λαοὶ Χριστοῦ τὰ γενέθλια* / "Let us celebrate beforehand, O ye peoples, the Nativity of Christ", transferred from Dec 20); at "Glory": *Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν*; at "Both now and ever": *Σπήλαιον εὐτρεπίζου* ("Prepare thyself, O cave"); at the Aposticha, 3 Forefeast Prosomoia (*Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ*) are chanted with Habakkuk psalm verses (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει* / "God shall come from Teman" and *Κύριε, εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου* / "O Lord, I have heard Thy report"); and the Dismissal Troparia are those of the Fathers (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*) and the Forefeast (*Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* / "Mary once, with aged Joseph, went to be enrolled"). At Sunday Matins (§ 8), instead of the Triadic Canon after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Canon *Κύματι θαλάσσης* appointed after Vespers of the 24th is sung; at "God is the Lord", the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion is restored alongside those of the Fathers and Forefeast; and the Kathismata integrate the Resurrection with Forefeast hymnography. Leaf p274 concludes mid-sentence at "then the Litany and the Hypakoe of the Tone, the...", resolving on physical leaf p275.

Physical leaf p275 (printed page 260) and facing English leaf p276 (printed page 261) complete Case 3 of the Sunday before the Nativity. The Typikon then opens the solemn Feast of the Nativity according to the Flesh of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ (December 25). Case 1 (§ 1) governs when the Feast of the Nativity occurs on a Friday. In this occurrence, Thursday (December 24) is the Paramony (Eve): in the morning, following daily Matins, the Great Hours (Royal Hours: First, Third, Sixth, and Ninth) are chanted, immediately followed by Great Vespers joined with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great. Leaf p276 concludes mid-sentence at § 2 ("Following the service of Matins, around the First Hour of the morning [7:00 a.m.],..."), resolving on physical leaf p277.

[^198]: Feast of the Nativity of Christ: The Royal Hours (First Hour Concluded & Third Hour, §§ 2–3). Physical leaf p277 (printed page 262) and facing English leaf p278 (printed page 263) provide the ceremonial ordotikon for the First and Third Royal Hours of the Nativity Eve when the Feast falls on Friday. At the First Hour (§ 2 concl.), the Patriarch or presiding Hierarch descends into the nave and begins the opening blessing (*Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν... Βασιλεῦ Οὐράνιε...*); three special psalms are read (Psalms 5, 44, and 45 LXX); following the Troparion *Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* and Theotokion, three idiomela are chanted antiphonally by the two choirs (*Βηθλεὲμ ἑτοιμάζου*, *Νῦν προφητικὴ πρόρρησις*, and *Τάδε λέγει Ἰωσήφ*); the First Canonarch reads the Prophecy (Micah 5:2–4, prophesying the birth in Bethlehem Ephrathah) and the Epistle (Hebrews 1:1–12, proclaiming the divine Sonship of Christ superior to the angels); and the Priest proclaims the Holy Gospel (Matthew 1:18–25, the Virginal Conception and birth of Emmanuel) before the Holy Doors. In an important rubrical note, Violakis specifies that during the chanting of the idiomela of the Third Hour, the Great Archdeacon (or Deacon, or Priest who read the Gospel) comes forth from the North Door dressed in a black mandyas, bearing a katzion (hand-censer with bells) preceded by a taper-bearer (Lambadouchos), and censes the people, a ceremony repeated at the Sixth and Ninth Hours by other deacons (in the absence of a Hierarch, the Priest censes robed in a phelonion). At the Third Hour (§ 3), following the psalms (Psalms 28, 66, and 50 LXX) and the Troparion of the Forefeast, the choirs chant the idiomela *Οὗτος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν* ("This is our God"), *Πρὸ τῆς γεννήσεως τῆς σῆς* ("Before Thy birth, O Lord"), and *Ἰωσὴφ εἰπὲ ἡμῖν* ("Tell us, Joseph"). Leaf p278 breaks off mid-sentence at "Then the...", resolving on physical leaf p279.

[^199]: Feast of the Nativity of Christ: The Royal Hours Concluded (Third Hour Concl., Sixth and Ninth Hours, §§ 3–5). Physical leaf p279 (printed page 264) and facing English leaf p280 (printed page 265) conclude the Royal Hours of the Nativity. At the Third Hour (§ 3 concl.), the Second Canonarch proclaims the Prophecy (Baruch 3:35–4:4, Christ appearing upon earth and conversing with men) and the Epistle (Galatians 3:23–29, the Law as tutor unto Christ, and adoption as sons through faith), and the Priest reads the Gospel (Luke 2:1–20, the Caesar Augustus census, the manger, and the Angelic Gloria heard by the shepherds). At the Sixth Hour (§ 4), after Psalms 71, 131, and 90 LXX, the idiomela are *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως* ("Come, ye faithful, let us be inspired divinely"), *Ἄκουε, οὐρανέ* ("Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth"), and *Δεῦτε, χριστοφόροι λαοί* ("Come, ye Christ-bearing peoples"); the Prophecy is Isaiah 7:10–16; 8:1–4, 9–10 (the virgin conceiving Emmanuel), the Epistle is Hebrews 2:11–18 (Christ partaking of flesh and blood to destroy the devil), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:1–12 (the Adoration of the Magi). At the Ninth Hour (§ 5), after Psalms 109, 110, and 85 LXX, the idiomela are *Ἐξεπλήττετο ὁ Ἡρώδης* ("Herod was struck with amazement") and *Ὅτε Ἰωσήφ, Παρθένε* ("When Joseph, O Virgin"); then the Canonarch stands in the midst of the nave facing east and solemnly chants the celebrated idiomelon *Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχων κτίσιν* ("Today He Who holds all creation in the hollow of His hand is born of a Virgin") in Gospel recitative style thrice, continuing with the strophes, repeating thrice *Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὴν γέννησιν, Χριστέ* ("We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ"), and once *Δεῖξον ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ θεῖά σου Θεοφάνεια* ("Show us also Thy divine Theophany"), whereupon the choirs repeat the idiomelon melodiously; the Prophecy is Isaiah 9:6–7 (Unto us a Child is born), the Epistle is Hebrews 2:1–10 (Jesus crowned with glory and honor), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:13–23 (the Flight into Egypt and Slaughter of the Holy Innocents). In Note 3, Violakis explains that historically the Typika were read after the Ninth Hour, but in modern practice are omitted to transition directly to Great Vespers with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.

Paragraph 21 assigns the Apodosis to Friday, December 31. Paragraph 22 introduces Situation Three (Γ΄), where December 25 falls on Sunday: on Friday morning, the Royal Hours alone are sung without Divine Liturgy, using the Troparion *Ἑτοιμάζου, Βηθλεέμ* ("Prepare, Bethlehem"), since *Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* ("Mary was registered once in a census") is reserved for the immediate Paramony.

[^208]: Situation Three Continued: Friday Evening Forefeast Vespers (§ 23); Saturday Paramony Matins and Liturgy (§ 24); Saturday Evening Great Festal Vespers (§ 25); Sunday Festal Matins and Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great (§ 26); Transfer of Sunday after the Nativity to Monday (§ 26 note). Physical leaf p297 (printed page 282) and facing English leaf p298 (printed page 283) continue Situation Three (Nativity on Sunday). On Friday evening (§ 23), daily Vespers is sung from the Menaion, followed after *Νῦν ἀπολύεις* by the Forefeast Canon (*Κύματι θαλάσσης* / "Waves of the sea") and the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion *Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* ("Mary was registered once in a census"). On Saturday morning (§ 24), Matins is sung with Canons read plain, Heirmos of Ode 8 chanted, Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*), Forefeast Exapostilaria, and Praises (*Ὦ τῶν ὑπὲρ νοῦν* / "What mysteries beyond understanding"); Divine Liturgy features the daily Antiphons (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι* / "It is good to give praise unto the Lord", Psalm 91:2 LXX), Entrance Hymn *ὁ ἐν ἁγίοις θαυμαστός* ("Who art wondrous in Thy saints"), Forefeast Dismissal Troparion, Epistle and Gospel of the Saturday before the Nativity, and Communion Verse Psalm 64:5 LXX (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω* / "Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen"). On Saturday evening (§ 25), Great Festal Vespers of the Nativity is chanted with 6 Stichira Idiomela (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*), Gospel Entrance, 8 Old Testament Readings, and immediately following the 8th reading (without the Litany) the Epistle and Gospel are proclaimed; then the Augmented Litany, Aposticha Idiomela (*Μέγα καὶ παράδοξον θαῦμα*), and Festal Dismissal Troparion thrice. On Sunday (§ 26), Festal Matins and the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great are celebrated as in Situation One. The concluding note explains that because the solitary Sunday between Nativity and Theophany coincides with January 1 (Circumcision of Christ and Saint Basil the Great), the commemoration of the Sunday after the Nativity (the Holy Ancestors of God) is transferred and joined to the Synaxis of the Theotokos on Monday, December 26.

Paragraphs 4–5 govern the order when January 1 falls on a Sunday: on Saturday evening (§ 4), at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira are sung (4 Resurrectional, 3 Festal Idiomela repeating the first, and 3 Prosomoia of Saint Basil); "Glory" of Saint Basil (*Σοφίας ἐραστής*); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone; Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon of the day, and 3 Old Testament Readings of the Feast; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory" of Saint Basil (*Ὁ τὴν χάριν τῶν θαυμάτων*), "Both now and ever" (*Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη ὁ πανάγαθος Θεός*); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Saint Basil (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν*), Circumcision (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*), and Dismissal. On Sunday Matins (§ 5 opening): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon and Lite of Saint Basil; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη*; Triadic hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Trisagion Prayers; Troparion *Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*; Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Polyeleos; Kathismata: one Resurrectional, one of Saint Basil, and one of the Feast at the first and second stichologia; at the third stichologia, those of the Menaion in order; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection, Circumcision, and Saint Basil.

[^217]: January 1 falling on Sunday Concluded: Matins (§ 5 concl.) and Divine Liturgy (§ 6); and Sunday before Theophany: Situation One: January 2, 3, or 4 (Saturday Vespers § 1 and Sunday Matins § 2 opening). Physical leaf p315 (printed page 300) and facing English leaf p316 (printed page 301) conclude the Sunday order for January 1 and open the rubrics for the Sunday before Theophany. At Sunday Matins (§ 5 concl.), Canons of the Resurrection, Circumcision, and Saint Basil are sung with 4 troparia each; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, Kathismata of Saint Basil and the Feast; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of Saint Basil, Menologion of the day; double Katavasiai of Theophany (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε* and *Στείβει θαλάσσης*); Morning Gospel order; Ode 9 of both Feast and Saint with their Megalynaria and both Katavasiai of Ode 9; Exapostilaria: Resurrectional, Saint Basil, Feast; Praises: 4 Resurrectional and 4 Festal Stichira; "Glory" of Saint Basil (*Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις*), "Both now and ever" (*Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ*), Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. At the Divine Liturgy on Sunday (§ 6): Antiphons of the Circumcision, with Second Antiphon refrain *Ὁ σαρκὶ περιτμηθείς*; Little Entrance with Sunday introit *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*; Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Circumcision, Saint Basil, Temple Patron; Kontakion *Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Κύριος*; Epistle of Saint Basil (Colossians 2:8–12), Gospel of the Circumcision (Luke 2:20–21, 40–52); Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great; at the Diptychs, Megalynarion of Saint Basil; Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX; Dismissal Troparion *Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*, and Dismissal. The Sunday before Theophany (Κυριακὴ πρὸ τῶν Φώτων), Situation One (§§ 1–2), covers the case when the Sunday occurs on January 2, 3, or 4: on Saturday evening (§ 1), following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and Psalter Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried" 10 Stichira are sung (6 Resurrectional, 4 Forefeast Idiomela from January 2 *Προεόρτια ᾄσματα*); "Glory" (*Ἔρχεται πρὸς Ἰορδάνην* / "He cometh unto Jordan"); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone; Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory... Both now and ever...": Forefeast Doxastikon from January 2 (*Ἰωάννη Βαπτιστά* / "O John the Baptist"); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Forefeast *Ἑτοιμάζου, Ζαβουλών* ("Prepare, O Zebulun"), and Dismissal. On Sunday Matins (§ 2 opening): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon and Triadic hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Trisagion Prayers; Dismissal Troparion *Ἑτοιμάζου, Ζαβουλών*; Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion twice and Forefeast once; Psalter and Amomos (Kathisma 17 / Psalm 118 LXX); Resurrectional Kathismata in order, Evlogitaria...

[^218]: Sunday before Theophany: Situation One Concluded (Matins § 2 concl., Divine Liturgy § 3) and Situation Two: Sunday before Theophany falling on Paramony, January 5 (Saturday Vespers § 4, Sunday Matins § 5 opening). Physical leaf p317 (printed page 302) and facing English leaf p318 (printed page 303) complete Situation One and commence Situation Two. Sunday Matins for Situation One continues (§ 2 concl.) with the Hypakoe of the Tone, Anavathmoi, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection and Forefeast; after Ode 3, Kathisma *Ἀόρατε Θεέ* ("Invisible God") once; after Ode 6, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, Menologion of the day; Katavasiai of Theophany (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα*); Morning Gospel order; Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*); Exapostilaria: Resurrectional and Forefeast *Πῶς ῥεῖθρά σε ποτάμια* ("How shall river streams receive Thee"); Praises: 4 Resurrectional and 4 Forefeast Stichira (*Αἱ ἀγγελικαὶ προπορεύεσθε δυνάμεις* / "O angelic hosts, go before"); "Glory": Morning Eothinon Doxastikon; "Both now and ever": *Ὑπερευλογημένη*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. Situation Two (§§ 4–5) applies when the Sunday before Theophany falls on January 5, the Eve (Paramony) of the Feast: on Saturday evening (§ 4), at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira are sung (6 Resurrectional, 4 Forefeast Idiomela *Προεόρτια ᾄσματα* [the Greek text contains a print duplication 'Προεόρτια α΄ Προεόρτια ᾄσματα', emended to 4 Forefeast Stichira as witnessed in the English column]); "Glory" (*Ἔρχεται πρὸς Ἰορδάνην*); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone; Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory... Both now and ever...": Forefeast Doxastikon from January 3 (*Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ* / "In the River Jordan"); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Forefeast *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε* ("The Jordan formerly turned back"), and Dismissal. On Sunday Matins (§ 5 opening): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon, Triadic hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*, Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Resurrectional Troparion twice, Forefeast once; Psalter and Amomos; Resurrectional Kathismata in order, Evlogitaria, Hypakoe of the Tone, Anavathmoi, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection and Forefeast (*Χριστὸς μολεῖ πρὸς τὸ βάπτισμα* / "Christ cometh unto baptism") with Verse "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos...

[^219]: Sunday before Theophany: Situation Two Concluded (Matins § 5 concl., Divine Liturgy § 6), Great Blessing of the Waters on Paramony; and Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6): Situation One: Feast falling on Friday (Royal Hours on Thursday, Vespers and Liturgy of Saint Basil § 1). Physical leaf p319 (printed page 304) and facing English leaf p320 (printed page 305) conclude the Sunday before Theophany and commence the Feast of the Holy Theophany of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ. Sunday Matins of Situation Two concludes (§ 5 concl.): after Ode 3, Kathisma *Ὁ μέγας ὑετός* ("The great rain" from January 5); after Ode 6, Kontakion of the Forefeast *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*, Ikos, Menologion of the day; Katavasiai *Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα*; Morning Gospel order; Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*); Exapostilaria: Resurrectional and Forefeast *Πῶς ῥεῖθρά σε ποτάμια*; Praises: 4 Resurrectional and 4 Forefeast Stichira (*Ἰδοὺ ὁ Βασιλεύς* / "Behold the King"); "Glory": Forefeast Doxastikon *Ἰωάννη Βαπτιστά*; "Both now and ever": *Ὑπερευλογημένη*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 6): Typika and Beatitudes (4 of Tone, 4 from Ode 6 of Forefeast Canon); Entrance with Resurrectional Troparion, Forefeast Troparion *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*, Temple Patron, Kontakion *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*; Epistle (2 Timothy 4:5–8) and Gospel (Mark 1:1–8) of the Sunday before Theophany; at "Especially": *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*. Immediately following the Prayer Behind the Ambon and *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου* ("Blessed be the name of the Lord"), the clergy proceed to the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters (Μέγας Ἁγιασμός): the choir chants the Idiomela *Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* ("The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), and the office is performed according to the Menaion; Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan") and Kontakion *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*; during the blessing and sprinkling of the faithful with holy water, the Second Choir chants the Idiomelon *᾿Ανυμνήσωμεν οἱ πιστοί* ("Let us, the faithful, praise"), followed by the Dismissal. At the trapeza, wine and olive oil are permitted in honor of the Sunday, relaxing the strict fast otherwise observed on the Eve of Theophany. The Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) opens with Situation One (when January 6 falls on a Friday, § 1): on Thursday morning (January 5), following prescribed Matins, the Royal Hours alone are sung according to the order of the Eve of the Nativity (referencing Christmas Situation One § 2). Great Vespers joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great with the Great Blessing of the Waters at the conclusion of the Liturgy are celebrated on Thursday afternoon according to the prescribed order.


## Cohort 33 Footnotes

[^220]: Eve of Holy Theophany (January 5) Concluded: Great Vespers Joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great, Old Testament Readings, and Great Blessing of the Waters (§ 2); and Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6): Friday Matins Opening (§ 3). Physical leaf p321 (printed page 306) and facing English leaf p322 (printed page 307) govern the festive eve and opening of Holy Theophany when January 6 falls on a Friday. Great Vespers joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great (§ 2) begins following the Dismissal of the Ninth Hour: the Deacon intones the opening blessing (*Εὐλόγησον, Δέσποτα* / "Bless, Master"), the Priest gives the doxological exclamation *Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Πατρός* ("Blessed is the kingdom of the Father..."), and the Patriarch (or presiding Hierarch) reads the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], followed by the Great Litany. At "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 6 Stichira are chanted: the 4 Idiomela of the Feast (*Τὸν φωτισμὸν ἡμῶν* / "Our illumination") repeating the first two; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Ὑπέκλινας κάραν τῷ Προδρόμῳ* ("Thou hast bowed Thy head unto the Forerunner"). The Little Entrance is made with the Holy Gospel Book, followed by *Φῶς ἱλαρόν* ("O Gladsome Light") and the thirteen Old Testament Readings of the Eve. Following Reading 3 (Genesis 1:1–13: *Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός* / "In the beginning God created"), the First Choir intones the Troparion *Ἐπεφάνης ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ* ("Thou hast appeared in the world"), and the Second Choir responds with the choral refrain *Ἵνα φωτίσῃς τοὺς ἐν σκότει καθημένους, Φιλάνθρωπε, δόξα σοι* ("To give light to those who sit in darkness; O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!"), sung alternately between the verses of Psalm 66 LXX until the Canonarch concludes. Following Reading 6 (4 Kingdoms 2:6–14 LXX / 2 Kings 2:6–14: *Εἶπεν Ἠλίας τῷ Ἐλισσαιέ* / "And Elijah said unto Elisha"), the Second Choir intones the Troparion *Ἁμαρτωλοῖς καὶ τελώναις* ("Unto sinners and tax-collectors"), and the choral refrain *Ποῦ γὰρ εἶχε τὸ φῶς σου λάμψαι* ("Where indeed should Thy light have shone...") is alternated between the verses of Psalm 92 LXX. Following Reading 13 (4 Kingdoms 5:1–14 LXX / 2 Kings 5:1–14: *Παραγένετο Νεεμὰν βασιλέως Ἀσσυρίων* / "So Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria [printed Ἀσσυρίων]"), the Small Litany is intoned, the Trisagion Hymn is chanted, followed by the Epistle (1 Corinthians 9:19–27), "Alleluia", and the Holy Gospel (Luke 3:1–18) proclaimed from the ambo, followed by the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great. The Communion Verse is Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* / "Praise the Lord from the heavens"), followed by *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν* ("We have seen the true light"). After the Prayer behind the Ambon, the clergy proceed to the solea for the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters (*Μέγας Ἁγιασμός*): the choirs chant the Idiomela *Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* ("The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), and the office is celebrated according to the Menaion; during the sprinkling of the faithful, the Second Choir sings the Idiomelon *Ἀνυμνήσωμεν οἱ πιστοί* ("Let us, the faithful, praise"), followed by the solemn festal Dismissal with its proper characteristic incipit: *Ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθῆναι καταδεξάμενος διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν* ("May He Who deigned to be baptized by John in the Jordan for our salvation, Christ our true God..."). The rubrics prescribe xerophagy (*ξηροφαγία*, strict fast without wine or oil) at table on this eve. Paragraph 3 opens Friday Matins for the feast: following Psalm 50 [LXX], the Lite and the Idiomela of the Aposticha (omitted on the eve due to the vigil Liturgy) are chanted; then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan"), and the Hexapsalmos; at "God is the Lord", the Dismissal Troparion is chanted thrice, followed by the Psalter Kathismata and the festal Polyeleos (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, Psalm 134 LXX; the printed English column incorrectly labels this Psalm 135 LXX by confusing Masoretic numbering).

[^221]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Friday Matins Gospel Order, Canons, and Festive Megalynaria of the Ninth Ode (§ 3 cont.). Physical leaf p323 (printed page 308) and facing English leaf p324 (printed page 309) provide the rubrical sequence of Friday Matins from the Kathismata through the Ninth Ode. Following the 3 Kathisma sedalia, the Anavathmoi of Tone 4 (First Antiphon *Ἐκ νεότητός μου* / "From my youth") are sung, followed by the Prokeimenon from Psalm 113:3 LXX (*Ἡ θάλασσα εἶδε καὶ ἔφυγεν, ὁ Ἰορδάνης ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω* / "The sea saw and fled, Jordan was driven back"). After *Πᾶσα πνοὴ αἰνεσάτω τὸν Κύριον* ("Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord"), the Matins Gospel is proclaimed (Mark 1:9–11), followed by Psalm 50 [LXX] read simply; "Glory": *Τὰ σύμπαντα σήμερον ἀγαλλιάσθω* ("Today let all things greatly rejoice"); "Both now and ever": the same; Verse: *Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός* (Ps. 50:3 LXX) and the Idiomelon *Θεὸς λόγος ἐπεφάνη ἐν σαρκί* ("God the Word appeared in the flesh"). Both Canons of the Feast are chanted with 4 troparia each, without verses except for "Glory... Both now and ever..." in each Ode: the First Canon by Saint Cosmas the Melodist in Tone 2 (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα* / "He uncovered the bottom of the deep") and the Second Iambic Canon by Saint John Damascene in Tone 2 (*Στείβει θαλάσσης* / "The Lord, working wonders"). After Ode 3, the Hypakoe *Ὅτε τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ σου* ("When at Thy manifestation"); after Ode 6, the Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον τῇ οἰκουμένῃ* ("Thou hast appeared today to the universe"), the Ikos, and the Menologion. Both Katavasiai are sung in full at each Ode. At Ode 9, the Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*) is not sung; instead, the festive Megalynaria (*Μεγαλυνάρια*) are appointed for each troparion. For the First Canon, four primary Megalynaria are given: (1) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν ἄνω στρατευμάτων* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her that is more honorable than the heavenly hosts"); (2) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ἐλθόντα βαπτισθῆναι* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him Who hath come to be baptized in the Jordan"); (3) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ὑπὸ Προδρόμου τὸ βάπτισμα αἰτοῦντα [λαβόντα]* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him Who asketh [receiveth] baptism from the Forerunner"); (4) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐκ τῆς Πατρῴας φωνῆς μαρτυρηθέντα* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him to Whom the voice of the Father bore witness"). Three additional bracketed Megalynaria marked with asterisks are preserved from the modern printed Athenian Menaion tradition (ed. Phos, 1960; Apostoliki Diakonia, 1991), although absent from the classical textus receptus of the Violakis Typikon: (5) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἕνα τῆς Τριάδος, κλίναντα τὸν αὐχένα, καὶ βάπτισμα λαβόντα* ("Magnify, O my soul, One of the Trinity Who bowed His head and received baptism"); (6) *Προφῆτα, δεῦρο πρός με, ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα, καὶ βάπτισόν με τάχος* ("O Prophet, come unto Me: stretch out thy hand and baptize Me swiftly"); (7) *Προφῆτα, ἄφες ἄρτι, καὶ βάπτισόν με θέλων· πληρῶσαι καὶ γὰρ ἦλθον, πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην* ("O Prophet, suffer it to be so now, and baptize Me willing: for I have come to fulfill all righteousness"). For the Second Iambic Canon, five Megalynaria are provided: (1) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, κλίνει τὸν αὐχένα, χειρὶ τῇ τοῦ Προδρόμου* ("Today the Master bows His head beneath the hand of the Forerunner"); (2) *Σήμερον Ἰωάννης, βαπτίζει τὸν Δεσπότην, ἐν ῥείθροις Ἰορδάνου* ("Today John baptizes the Master in the streams of the Jordan"); and three bracketed Menaion additions: (3) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, νάμασιν ἐνθάπτει, βροτῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν* ("Today the Master buries in the waters the sin of mortal man"); (4) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, ἄνωθεν μαρτυρεῖται, Υἱὸς ἠγαπημένος* ("Today the Master receives testimony from on high, that He is the beloved Son"); (5) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, ἦλθεν ἁγιάσαι, τὴν φύσιν τῶν ὑδάτων* ("Today the Master has come to sanctify the nature of the waters").

[^222]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Conclusion of Matins Ode 9, Praises, Great Doxology, and Great Blessing of the Waters Rite (§ 3 concl.). Physical leaf p325 (printed page 310) and facing English leaf p326 (printed page 311) conclude the Ninth Ode and detail the Great Blessing of the Waters celebrated at the climax of the Great Doxology. Ode 9 concludes with the final Megalynaria: *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, τὸ βάπτισμα λαμβάνει, ὑπὸ χειρὸς Προδρόμου* ("Today the Master receives baptism at the hand of the Forerunner"); "Glory": *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τῆς τρισυποστάτου, καὶ ἀδιαιρέτου, θεότητος τὸ κράτος* ("Magnify, O my soul, the power of the Godhead in three Persons and undivided"); "Both now and ever": *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν λυτρωσαμένην, ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κατάρας* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her who hath delivered us from the curse"). Matins continues with the Exapostilarion chanted thrice; at the Praises: 6 Idiomela (*Φῶς ἐκ φωτός* / "Light from Light"); "Glory": *Νάματα Ἰορδάνεια* ("O Savior, Who clothedst Thyself with the waters of Jordan"); "Both now and ever": *Σήμερον ὁ Χριστός* ("Today Christ"), and the Great Doxology. In the Great Doxology, an ancient Constantinopolitan rubrical custom replaces the customary opening verse *Δόξα σοι τῷ δείξαντι τὸ φῶς* ("Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light") with the concluding refrain of the Theotokion: "We who have been enlightened cry aloud: Glory to God made manifest, Who hath appeared upon earth and brought light unto the world." Immediately following the third repetition of the Trisagion (*Ἅγιος ἀθάνατος, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*) at the end of the Doxology, the clergy and choirs transition directly into the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters: the choirs chant the 3 Idiomela of Saint Sophronius of Jerusalem (*Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* / "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Πρὸς τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ* ("At the voice of one crying in the wilderness"). The Priest exits through the Holy Doors carrying the Precious Cross on his head, preceded by candle-bearers and Deacons; the Patriarch (or presiding Hierarch), vested in epitrachilion and small omophorion, descends from his Throne to the center of the temple where the water vessel has been prepared. The Canonarch reads the three Prophecies (Isaiah 35:1–10; 55:1–13; 12:3–6), followed by the Epistle (1 Corinthians 10:1–4) and the Gospel (Mark 1:9–11) proclaimed by the Patriarch. Following the polychronion (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), the Great Archdeacon intones the Great Litany of the Blessing while the Patriarch recites silently the secret prayer *Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ* ("O Lord Jesus Christ"), culminating in the aloud exclamation *Τριὰς ὑπερούσιε* ("O Trinity transcending essence") and the great festive prayer *Μέγας εἶ, Κύριε, καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου* ("Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous are Thy works"), repeated thrice with the choral acclamation *Δόξα σοι, Κύριε, δόξα σοι!* ("Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thee!"). A critical apparatus note in both Greek and English facsimile columns addresses a numbering error in the 1888 edition, where Violakis misnumbered this footnote as footnote 4 instead of 1; the note documents the pastoral practice emerging in parish churches of delaying the Great Blessing of the Waters until after the Divine Liturgy to prevent disorder and accommodate late-arriving faithful.

[^223]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Conclusion of the Great Blessing of the Waters and Divine Liturgy Antiphons 1 & 2 (§ 4 opening). Physical leaf p327 (printed page 312) and facing English leaf p328 (printed page 313) conclude the solemn sanctification of waters and commence the festal Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. Following the thrice-repeated prayer *Μέγας εἶ, Κύριε*, the celebrant immerses the Precious Cross into the water vessel three times with the sprinkler (*ἁγιαστήρ*), chanting each time the Dismissal Troparion of Theophany: *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan"), repeated by each choir. He then sprinkles the congregation cruciformly with the newly consecrated water while chanting the Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον τῇ οἰκουμένῃ* ("Thou hast appeared today to the universe"). As the Patriarch ascends the Throne amidst choral acclamations (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), he sprinkles the concelebrating Hierarchs and clergy; during this sprinkling, the choirs chant slowly and melodiously the Troparion from Ode 8 of the Canon: *Τριάδος ἡ φανέρωσις* ("The manifestation of the Trinity"). The Second Choir then chants the Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom commences immediately. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 4), the special festive Antiphons of Theophany are chanted in Tone 2: First Antiphon verses from Psalm 113:1, 2, 3, 5 LXX (*Ἐν ἐξόδῳ Ἰσραὴλ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, οἴκου Ἰακώβ* / "When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarian people"; *Ἐγενήθη Ἰουδαία ἁγίασμα αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ ἐξουσία αὐτοῦ* / "Judea became His sanctuary, and Israel His dominion"; *Ἡ θάλασσα εἶδε καὶ ἔφυγεν· ὁ Ἰορδάνης ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω* / "The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back"; *Τί σοί ἐστι θάλασσα, ὅτι ἔφυγες; καὶ σὺ Ἰορδάνη, ὅτι ἐστράφης εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω;* / "What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? And thou, Jordan, that thou didst turn back?"); refrain: *Ταῖς πρεσβείαις τῆς Θεοτόκου, Σῶτερ, σῶσον ἡμᾶς* ("Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us"). Second Antiphon verses from Psalm 114:1, 2, 3, 5 LXX (*Ἠγάπησα, ὅτι εἰσακούσεται Κύριος τῆς φωνῆς τῆς δεήσεώς μου* / "I am well pleased that the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer"; *Ὅτι ἔκλινε τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ ἐμοί, καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις μου ἐπικαλέσομαι* / "For He hath inclined His ear unto me, and in my days will I call upon Him"; *Περιέσχον με ὠδῖνες θανάτου, κίνδυνοι ᾅδου εὕροσάν με* / "The pangs of death compassed me, the perils of Hades found me; I found tribulation and sorrow"; *Ἐλεήμων ὁ Κύριος καὶ δίκαιος, καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐλεεῖ* / "Merciful is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful").

[^224]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Concluded: Divine Liturgy Antiphon 3, Little Entrance, Epistle, Gospel, and Dismissal (§ 4 concl.); and Synaxis of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John (January 7): Friday Vespers (§ 5). Physical leaf p329 (printed page 314) and facing English leaf p330 (printed page 315) conclude the festal Divine Liturgy of Theophany and commence the post-festal Synaxis of the Forerunner celebrated on the following day. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 4 concl.), the Second Antiphon concludes with the refrain *Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθείς, ψάλλοντάς σοι, Ἀλληλούϊα* ("Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized by John in the Jordan, who sing to Thee: Alleluia"), followed by *Ὁ Μονογενὴς Υἱὸς καὶ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ* ("Only-begotten Son and Immortal Word of God"). The Third Antiphon is chanted in Tone 1 to verses from Psalm 117:1–4 LXX (*Ἐξομολογεῖσθε τῷ Κυρίῳ, ὅτι ἀγαθός, ὅτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ* / "O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endureth forever"; *Εἰπάτω δὴ οἶκος Ἰσραήλ...* / "Let the house of Israel now say..."; *Εἰπάτω δὴ οἶκος Ἀαρών...* / "Let the house of Aaron now say..."; *Εἰπάτωσαν δὴ πάντες οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν Κύριον...* / "Let all that fear the Lord now say..."); refrain: Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*. At the Little Entrance, the festive Introit Verse is chanted from Psalm 117:26, 27 LXX: *Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν. Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθείς, ψάλλοντάς σοι, Ἀλληλούϊα* ("Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord; the Lord is God, and hath appeared unto us. Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized by John in the Jordan, who sing to Thee: Alleluia"). Troparia: Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον*. Instead of the Trisagion Hymn, the baptismal hymn is chanted: *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε. Ἀλληλούϊα* ("All of you who have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia", Galatians 3:27). The Epistle of the Feast is Titus 2:11–14; 3:4–7; the Gospel is Matthew 3:13–17. At "Especially", instead of the Axion Estin, the Heirmos of Ode 9 is chanted: *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου τὴν τιμιωτέραν καὶ ἐνδοξοτέραν τῶν ἄνω στρατευμάτων. Ἀπορεῖ πᾶσα γλῶσσα* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her that is more honorable and more glorious than the heavenly hosts. Every tongue is at a loss to praise Thee worthily..."). The Communion Verse is Titus 2:11: *Ἐπεφάνη ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ σωτήριος πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις* ("The grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared unto all men"); instead of *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and the Dismissal. On Friday evening (§ 5), the Synaxis of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John (*Ἡ Σύναξις τοῦ τιμίου Προδρόμου*) is celebrated at Great Vespers: after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 6 Stichira are chanted: 3 Idiomela of the Feast (*Τὸν φωτισμὸν ἡμῶν*) and 3 Prosomoia of the Forerunner (*Πανεύφημε Πρόδρομε Χριστοῦ*); "Glory": *Ἔνσαρκε λύχνε* ("O torch incarnate"); "Both now and ever": *Θεὸς λόγος ἐπεφάνη ἐν σαρκί* ("God the Word appeared in the flesh"). Entrance with *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, followed by the Great Prokeimenon in Tone 7 from Psalm 113:11 LXX: *Ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐν τῇ γῇ, πάντα ὅσα ἠθέλησεν ἐποίησεν* ("Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He hath willed, He hath done") with its four verses. At the Aposticha: 3 Prosomoia Stichira beginning *Ὡς εἶδέ σε Δέσποτα* ("When he saw Thee, O Master"); "Glory": *Ὡς τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐραστής* ("As a lover of the Spirit"); "Both now and ever": *Δεῦτε μιμησώμεθα* ("Come, let us imitate the wise virgins"); Dismissal Troparia: Theophany (*Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*), and Forerunner (*Μνήμη δικαίου μετ’ ἐγκωμίων* / "The memory of the righteous is celebrated with hymns of praise").

At § 22: Saturday Matins opens following the Midnight Service, with the reading of the Psalter Kathismata, followed by the Canons of the Forefeast and of the Saints.

Scholarly Rubrical Decree of Patriarch Constantine I the Byzantine concerning the Praises on Sundays: Explains the standard rubrical canon prescribing the Resurrectional Eothinon Doxastikon at "Glory..." at the Praises on ordinary Sundays of the year, but establishes that for the great Ecumenical Doctors Gregory the Theologian and John Chrysostom, out of just debt to their pastoral guidance and immortal writings illuminating the Catholic Church, when their commemorations coincide with a Sunday outside the Triodion, the Doxastikon of the Saint is chanted instead of the Eothinon, especially in the Great Church of Constantinople. [^250]: Feast of the Meeting of our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ (Hypapante, February 2) — Case I: Weekday Celebration (Conclusion of Matins: Ode 9 Megalynaria): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p381 (printed page 366) and facing English leaf p382 (printed page 367). Following the initial Megalynarion *Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι* (inaugurated on leaf p380), the ninth ode of the Canon of the Meeting (composed by Saint Cosmas of Maiuma and embellished by the Byzantine sticheraric tradition) presents an alphabetical series of ten nine-syllable/twelve-syllable Megalynaria addressed alternately to the Theotokos, Christ, and the Righteous Symeon: (1) concluding verse of initial incipit: *Ἀγγέλοις καὶ βροτοῖς, Μητροπάρθενε ἁγνή* ["...unto angels and mortal men, O pure Virgin Mother"]; (2) *Ἀγκαλίζεται χερσίν, ὁ Πρεσβύτης Συμεών* ["Symeon the Elder takes in his arms the Maker of the Law and Master of all"]; (3) *Βουληθεὶς ὁ Πλαστουργός, ἵνα σώσῃ τὸν Ἀδάμ* ["The Creator, wishing to save Adam, took up His dwelling in thy pure and virgin womb"]; (4) *Γένος ἅπαν τῶν βροτῶν, μακαρίζει σε Ἁγνή* ["All the race of mortals blesseth thee, O Pure Virgin, and in faith glorifieth thee as Mother of God"]; (5) *Δεῦτε ἴδετε Χριστόν, τὸν Δεσπότην τοῦ παντός* ["Come and behold Christ, the Master of all, Whom Symeon beareth today in the temple"]; (6) *Ἐπιβλέπεις πρὸς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ποιεῖς τρέμειν αὐτήν* ["Thou lookest upon the earth and makest it tremble; how then can I, aged and weary, hold Thee in mine arms?"]; (7) *Ζήσας ἔτη Συμεών, ἕως εἶδε τὸν Χριστόν* ["Symeon lived for many years until he beheld Christ, and cried aloud unto Him: 'Now do I seek release'"]; (8) *Ἡ λαβὶς ἡ μυστική, ἡ τὸν ἄνθρακα Χριστόν* ["Thou art the mystic tongs, Mary, who hast conceived in thy womb Christ the live Coal" — drawing upon Isaiah 6:6]; (9) *Θέλων ἐνηνθρώπησας, ὁ προάναρχος Θεός* ["Of Thine own will Thou didst become man, O God without beginning, and art brought into the temple, forty days of age"]; (10) *Κατελθόντ’ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τὸν Δεσπότην τοῦ παντός* ["Symeon the priest received the Master of all, Who came down from heaven"]. Rubrical expansion of the 4 Troparia of Ode 9 to 6 with their proper appointed Megalynaria: Troparion 1 *Ἐν νόμῳ σκιᾷ* with Megalynarion *Λάμπρυνόν μου τὴν ψυχήν*; Troparion 2 with Megalynarion *Μητροπάρθενε ἁγνή, τί προσφέρεις*; Troparion 3 *Τοῖς πρὶν νεογνῶν* with Megalynarion *Νῦν ἀπόλυσιν ζητῶ*; Troparion 4 with Megalynarion *Ὃν οἱ ἄνω λειτουργοί*; Doxastikon (*Δόξα*) with Triadikon *Ἡ τῇ φύσει μὲν μονάς* ["O Thou Who art by nature One, but in Persons Three..."] paired with Megalynarion *Ἀπέδωκάς μοι*; and Theotokion (*Καὶ νῦν*) *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς* ["O Theotokos, Hope of all Christians, shelter, guard, and preserve those whose hope is in thee..."] paired with Megalynarion *Ἱεροπρεπῶς ἀνθωμολογεῖτο*.

Paragraph 17 completes Sunday Matins for the festal Apodosis within the Triodion: after Psalm 50 LXX, Triadic Canon, and Triodion Litiya Idiomelon (if present), Kathismata across three Stichologiai (Resurrectional paired with festal); Canons of Resurrection, Triodion, and Feast; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion, Triodion and festal Kathismata; after Ode 6, Triodion Kontakion/Ikos and Menologion; Katavasiai *Χέρσον ἀβυσσοτόκον*, festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*) with Troparia and Katavasia *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς. . . Paragraph 19 resolves Situation III: when the Feast of the Meeting coincides with Meatfare Saturday (the Saturday of Souls): the ancestral rubrics of the ancient Typika and the authoritative rulings of Patriarchs Constantios I (1830–1834) and Gregory VI (1835–1840, 1867–1871) mandate that the entire Office of the Souls be transferred to the preceding Saturday (the Saturday before the Sunday of the Prodigal Son), so that the Feast of the Meeting may be celebrated on its own day without displacement or abbreviation according to the primary rubrics of §§ 1–3.

[^258]: Variable Calendrical Cases for the Apodosis of the Meeting (Cases 1–5) and Cheesefare Sunday Evening Vespers (§ 20 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p397 (printed page 382) and facing English leaf p398 (printed page 383). The Typikon provides a rigorous 5-case combinatorial matrix for fixing the date of the Apodosis of the Meeting based upon its interaction with the movable pre-Lenten Triodion cycle: Case 1 [α΄]: Feast occurs between Sunday of Publican and Pharisee and Friday of that week -> Apodosis on regular 8th day (February 9); Case 2 [β΄]: Feast occurs between Saturday eve of Prodigal Son and Tuesday of Meatfare Week -> Apodosis celebrated early on Friday before the Saturday of Souls, because the ancestral Office of the Dead on Meatfare Saturday is inviolable and cannot be displaced for an Apodosis; Case 3 [γ΄]: Feast occurs between Wednesday of Meatfare Week and Saturday of Souls -> Apodosis postponed to Tuesday of Cheesefare Week; Case 4 [δ΄]: Feast occurs between Meatfare Sunday and Tuesday of Cheesefare Week -> Apodosis on Friday of Cheesefare Week; Case 5 [ε΄]: Feast occurs between Wednesday and Saturday of Cheesefare Week -> Apodosis celebrated on Cheesefare Sunday per §§ 16–18. When the Feast itself falls on Cheesefare Sunday (celebrated per §§ 11–13), the Apodosis is celebrated that same evening at Forgiveness Vespers (§ 20): "Lord, I have cried" combines 3 Stichira of the Feast and 3 of the Righteous Symeon; Great Prokeimenon *Μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς* (Psalm 68:18 LXX); Aposticha Idiomelon *Ἔλαμψεν ἡ χάρις σου* and festal Theotokion; proper festal Dismissal followed immediately by the Forgiveness rite without the customary priestly blessing *Δι’ εὐχῶν*.

[^259]: Cheesefare Sunday Evening Forgiveness Vespers Conclusion (§ 20 concl.) and Situation IV: Clean Monday Concurrence (§§ 21–22): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p399 (printed page 384) and facing English leaf p400 (printed page 385). Paragraph 20 concludes the Forgiveness Vespers rite marking the opening of Great Lent: following the festal Dismissal of the Meeting (omitting *Δι’ εὐχῶν*), the Choirs chant the penitential Troparion *Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*, 40 *Κύριε ἐλέησον*, *Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*, the Prayer of Saint Ephrem with Great Prostrations [Metanias], the Deacon/Priest litany *Εὐξώμεθα ὑπὲρ εἰρήνης τοῦ κόσμου*, and the hymn *Πάντων προστατεύεις* while clergy and faithful exchange the kiss of peace and mutual forgiveness, formally concluding the Apodosis of the Feast. Paragraphs 21–22 formulate Situation IV: when February 2 coincides with Clean Monday (the first day of Great Lent): on Cheesefare Sunday evening at Vespers (§ 21), "Lord, I have cried" combines 3 Triodion fasting Idiomela (*Ἐγκρατείᾳ τὴν σάρκα*) and 3 festal Stichira (*Λέγε Συμεών*), Great Prokeimenon Psalm 133:1 LXX (*Ἰδοὺ δὴ εὐλογεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*), Old Testament Readings of the Feast, and festal Aposticha; on Clean Monday at Matins (§ 22), the festal Litiya and "God is the Lord" lead into Kathismata across three Stichologiai combining Triodion fasting hymns (*Τῆς νηστείας τῇ θείᾳ ἀπαρχῇ*, *Τὴν πάνσεπτον ἐγκράτειαν*) with festal Kathismata; Anavathmoi (Antiphon 1 of Tone 4), Prokeimenon (Psalm 44:18 LXX), and festal Morning Gospel; Canon to 6 with festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*) and festal Exapostilarion *Ἐν πνεύματι τῷ Ἱερῷ* thrice; Praises combining festal Stichira Prosomia *Νόμον τὸν ἐν γράμματι* and festal Doxastikon *Ὁ ἐν χερσὶ πρεσβυτικαῖς*, concluding with the Great Doxology.

Paragraph 28 governs Tuesday of the Second Week per §§ 13–15. The concluding rubrical note outlines the occurrence envelope of St. Charalampos: falling between the Sunday of the Publican and Pharisee and Tuesday of the Second Week of Great Lent per the Heortodromion table. The monument then introduces the feast of February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Honorable Glorious Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John (*Ἡ α΄ καὶ β΄ εὕρεσις τῆς τιμίας κεφαλῆς τοῦ Προδρόμου*).

The rubric notes that on Friday of the Second, Third, and Fourth Weeks the same order is kept, omitting the Stichira of St. Theodore and chanting the day's Idiomelon twice, 4 Martyrika, and 4 of the Martyrs. Paragraph 7 establishes Situation IV: when the feast falls on Saturday of the First Week (Theodore Saturday, commemorating the Miracle of the Kolyva): on Friday morning at Vespers, after Kathisma 18, 10 Stichira combine *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ* twice, 4 of the Martyrs, and 4 of St. Theodore; Doxastikon of St. Theodore *Ὀργάνῳ χρησάμενος*, first Theotokion of the Tone, Little Entrance with the censer, "O Gladsome Light", Readings, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, Presanctified Liturgy with Communion Verse Psalm 33:9 LXX (*Γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε*), and Dismissal.

[^284]: March 9: Commemoration of the Holy Forty Martyrs of Sebastea — Situation XII Conclusion (§ 21, Festal Range Note); March 25: The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos — Paramony Rubric and Situation I Opening (§ 1). The general rubric notes that the Feast of the Forty Martyrs can fall within the Triodion cycle between Wednesday of the First Week of Great Lent and Great and Holy Monday of Passion Week. For March 25 (The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos), the Paramony Rubric distinguishes cathedral/parish usage from monastic typika: when the Eve falls on Wednesday or Friday, parish churches do not celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy because they do not hold an all-night vigil (except on Great and Holy Tuesday and Wednesday), whereas monasteries celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy combined with Small Vespers according to ancient founder typika. Paragraph 1 establishes Situation I: when the Annunciation falls on Friday of the 3rd Week of Great Lent, on Wednesday morning at Vespers of the Presanctified, after Kathisma 18, at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira combine the day's Idiomelon twice, Martyrikon once, 3 Prosomia of the sequence of the Triodion, and 4 Forefeast Prosomia *Κεκρυμμένον μυστήριον*; Doxastikon *Εὐαγγελίζεται ὁ Γαβριὴλ*, Little Entrance with "O Gladsome Light", Readings of the day, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, and the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts follows in due order.

Paragraph 69 introduces Situation XXIII: concurrence on Holy and Great Friday or Holy and Great Saturday: the Feast is transferred and celebrated on Easter Sunday itself together with the Resurrection Office. Violakis transcribes the canonical decree of the Ecumenical Patriarchate: "The Holy and Great Church of Christ, having received this tradition from Patriarchs and Hierarchs from a century ago to the present, observing the disagreement and confusion occurring throughout all the churches in cities and villages, took thought especially concerning the great solemnity of the Annunciation. And indeed, for the cessation of the apparent anomaly, especially in the ears of the simple folk who do not perceive deeply the things of the Spirit, the Church ordained that, if the Feast falls on these two sorrowful days [Holy Friday or Holy Saturday], it should be transferred to the supreme day of Pascha itself named after the Lord. In order that joyous things may be sung and melodized together with joyous things, the Church by economy prevented the mixing of the bright with the sorrowful, in order also that no disharmony might be shown between: 'Today He is hung upon the tree' (*Σήμερον κρεμᾶται ἐπὶ ξύλου*) and: 'Today are the glad tidings of joy' (*Σήμερον χαρᾶς εὐαγγέλια*), and between: 'Pouring out tears of lamentation over Thee, O Pure One' (*Δακρυρρόους θρήνους ἐπὶ σὲ Ἁγνὴ*) and: 'Gabriel to the Virgin the glad tidings' (*Ὁ Γαβριὴλ τῇ Παρθένῳ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον*). But these provisions, as has been said, pertain only to the churches in cities and villages..."


## Cohort 52 Footnotes

[^315]: March 25: The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos — Situation XXIII Conclusion (§§ 69–70) and Situation XXIV Opening (§ 71): Patriarchal Decree Justification Regarding Monasteries, the Order of Annunciation Concurring on Great Saturday / Pascha (Holy Saturday Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great), and Opening of the Paschal Midnight Office. Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p511 (printed page 496) and facing English leaf p512 (printed page 497). Paragraph 69 concludes the canonical justification of the Ecumenical Patriarchate: while city and parish temples transfer the feast of the Annunciation to Easter Sunday when concurring on Great Friday or Great Saturday to prevent mixing sorrowful rites with joyful festal hymnody, the ancient Typika of the Holy Monasteries remain entirely unchanged, untouched, and unshakeable, out of reverence toward their venerable Founders and Fathers, and because of the distinct character and loftier spiritual asceticism of the monastic commonwealth. Paragraph 70 codifies the liturgical ordo when the Annunciation is transferred to Easter Sunday: on Holy and Great Saturday, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 3 Resurrection Stichira of Tone 1 (*Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχάς*), 3 Idiomela of the Triodion (*Σήμερον ὁ ᾅδης*), and 4 Prosomia of the Feast (*Βουλὴν προαιώνιον*); "Glory...": *Τὴν Σήμερον μυστικῶς*; "Both now and ever...": *Ἀπεστάλη ἐξ οὐρανοῦ*. Entrance with the Holy Gospel, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, and immediately without a Prokeimenon, four Old Testament Lessons: (1) Genesis 1:1–13; (2) Genesis 28:10–17 (of the Feast); (3) Jonah 1–4; and (4) Daniel 3:1–57 (the remaining 11 readings of the ancient vigil being omitted for brevity in parish usage). This critical editorial rubric confirms the hierarchy of feasts and concurs with Situation Seven of Saint John the Theologian (p. 556).

The rubrician specifies that if the feast of the Saint occurs on another day outside the period of the Pentecostarion, the service is chanted as prescribed in the Menaion: Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*, Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*, and Communion Hymn *Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν* [Ps. 18:5 LXX]. Note on calendar limits: the commemoration of Saint Constantine can fall within the Pentecostarion from Saturday of the Week of the Paralytic until the Sunday of All Saints; outside of the Pentecostarion, until Thursday of the first week after the Sunday of All Saints (see the Calendar Table of Feasts). May 25 begins with the Third Finding of the Head of the Forerunner. Situation One details concurrence on the Apodosis of Mid-Pentecost: § 1 details Vespers: 3 Stichira of the Feast and 3 of the Forerunner; "Glory...": of the Forerunner; "Both now and ever...": of the Feast; Aposticha of the Feast; "Glory...": of the Forerunner; "Both now and ever...": of the Feast. Dismissal Troparion of the Feast, that of the Forerunner, again that of the Feast, and Dismissal. § 2 opening details Matins: Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter reading and 17th Kathisma [Amomos]; Sessional Hymns of the Forerunner and of the Feast; Matins Gospel of the Forerunner according to the order of the Menaion.

Commemoration of August 2: Translation of the Relics of Saint Stephen: Paragraph 1 concludes: Aposticha Verses: *Δίκαιος ὡς φοῖνιξ ἀνθήσει* [Ps. 91:13 LXX] and *Πεφυτευμένος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ Κυρίου* [Ps. 91:14 LXX]; "Glory...": *Χαίροις ἐν Κυρίῳ Στέφανε μακάριε*; "Both now and ever...": *Θεοτόκε σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος . . . μετὰ τοῦ Ἀθλοφόρου*; *Νῦν ἀπολύεις*, and immediately begins the Order of the Paraklesis. Section: The Order of the Paraklesis (Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos throughout the Dormition Fast, August 1–14): The Patriarch (or Superior) recites Psalm 142 [LXX] *Κύριε εἰσάκουσον τῆς προσευχῆς μου* in a low voice [recto tono]; the Choirs chant "God is the Lord" four times in Tone 4, with *Τῇ Θεοτόκῳ ἐκτενῶς νῦν προσδράμωμεν*; "Glory...": Dismissal Troparion of the Patron Saint of the Church; "Both now and ever...": *Οὐ σιωπήσωμέν ποτε Θεοτόκε*; Psalm 50 [LXX] is read in a low voice. Then the Canon of the Small Paraklesis is chanted without Heirmoi, beginning immediately with *Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε σῶσον ἡμᾶς... Πολλοῖς συνεχόμενος πειρασμοῖς*, with 4 Troparia in each Ode. After Ode 3: *Διάσωσον ἀπὸ κινδύνων* and *Ἐπίβλεψον ἐν εὐμενείᾳ*; the Priest intones the Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*, with Choirs chanting *Κύριε ἐλέησον* 12 times (4 sets of 3); Sessional Hymn: *Πρεσβεία θερμή*, and the Second Choir begins Ode 4. After Ode 6: *Διάσωσον ἀπὸ κινδύνων* and *Ἄχραντε ἡ διὰ λόγου*; the Priest intones the Insistent Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*; Kontakion: *Προστασία τῶν χριστιανῶν*; Prokeimenon: *Μνησθήσομαι τοῦ ὀνόματός σου* [Ps. 44:18 LXX]; *Πᾶσα πνοή*, and Gospel of the Mother of God: *Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ* (Luke 1:39–49, 56); "Glory...": *Πάτερ, Λόγε, Πνεῦμα*; "Both now and ever...": *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*; Psalm 50 verse: *Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός*, and the Sticheron: *Μὴ καταπιστεύσῃς με ἀνθρωπίνῃ προστασίᾳ*, *Οὐδεὶς προστρέχων ἐπὶ σοί*, *Μεταβολὴ τῶν θλιβομένων*. Priest proclaims: *Σῶσον ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαόν σου*; Choirs sing *Κύριε ἐλέησον* 12 times; Prayer: *Ἐλέει καὶ οἰκτιρμοῖς*; Odes 7, 8, and 9 are chanted. After Ode 9: Megalynaria: *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν ὡς ἀληθῶς*, *Τὴν Ὑψηλοτέραν τῶν οὐρανῶν*, etc. During *Ἄλαλα τὰ χείλη τῶν ἀσεβῶν*, the Patriarch venerates the icon of the Theotokos and, returning to the Throne, blesses the people while the Choirs chant *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*; then the remaining Megalynaria: *Ψάλλομεν προθύμως σοι τὴν Ὠδήν*, of the Patron Saint of the Church, and *Πᾶσαι τῶν Ἀγγέλων αἱ στρατιαί*; Trisagion Prayers; Dismissal Troparion of the Saint: *Βασίλειον διάδημα*, and Theotokion: *Τὸ ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος ἀπόκρυφον*. Priest intones the Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*, *Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τοῦ διαφυλαχθῆναι...*; Choirs respond *Κύριε ἐλέησον*; Patriarch proclaims: *Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός*; Priest: *Σοφία*.

After Ode 9 of the Canon, the 4 Exaposteilaria *Ἀπόστολοι ἐκ περάτων*; at the third, the Patriarch venerates the icon of the Theotokos and, returning to the Throne, blesses the people (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*); then *Χρυσοπλοκώτατε πύργε*; the Trisagion Prayers, and instead of the Dismissal Troparion of the Saints (who have no Doxastikon), the three Penitential Troparia are chanted: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς Κύριε*, *Κύριε ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*, and *Τῆς εὐσπλαγχνίας τὴν πύλην*. If the Paraklesis is chanted on a Friday, the Penitential Troparia are replaced by: *Ἀπόστολοι, Μάρτυρες*, *Μνήσθητι Κύριε*, and *Μήτηρ Ἁγία*. After the Feast of the Transfiguration, the Dismissal Troparion of the Transfiguration is chanted instead. Original Printed Footnote 1: George Violakis documents that while the printed Horologion prescribes chanting the Megalynaria *Τὴν Ὑψηλοτέραν τῶν οὐρανῶν*, etc., after the Ninth Ode, and placing the Exaposteilaria *Ἀπόστολοι ἐκ περάτων* after the Trisagion in place of Dismissal Troparia, the Patriarchal practice of Constantinople strictly maintains the order noted above (Exaposteilaria immediately after Ode 9, and Penitential Troparia after the Trisagion).

Original Printed Footnote 4: George Violakis documents the patriarchal prohibition against the unauthorized chanting of Enkomia to the Theotokos: In certain parishes, where the Feast of the Dormition is celebrated with solemnity, an unauthorized practice arose—supposedly for the greater honor of the Theotokos—of chanting so-called Enkomia [Lamentations/Praises] after the Ninth Ode in imitation of the Matins of Great and Holy Saturday. The Great Church of Christ officially condemns and sternly forbids all such novelties and theatrical imitations.

Week of Cheesefare: On Monday morning, the Service of the day is chanted as in the Triodion. On Tuesday and Thursday evenings, after the Trisagion Prayers, we chant "O Theotokos Virgin" (*Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*) because no Divine Liturgy is celebrated on Wednesday or Friday; prostrations are made, then "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), "Glory... Both now and ever...", "More honorable than the Cherubim", and Dismissal. Footnote 4 of the Greek edition notes that the Holy Fathers did not hand down to celebrate either a complete Liturgy or a Presanctified Liturgy on Wednesday or Friday of Cheesefare week; if, however, an Afterfeast of the Meeting of the Lord (Hypapante) or the memory of a celebrated Saint occurs, the hymns of the Triodion are omitted and the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom is celebrated. After the Apodosis of the Meeting, at the commemorations of celebrated Saints occurring during this week, the Katavasiai sung are "I shall open my mouth" (*Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*) and the Kontakion "Protection of Christians" (*Προστασία τῶν χριστιανῶν*) (see § 26 of the Protheoria). Fasting Note: Throughout Cheesefare week, meat is forbidden, but cheese, eggs, and fish are permitted even on Wednesday and Friday.

[^404]: Triodion: Sunday of Cheesefare (Concl. Liturgy § 16; Forgiveness Vespers § 17). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p689 (printed page 674) and facing English leaf p690 (printed page 675). Sunday of Cheesefare: Paragraph 16 concludes the Divine Liturgy: at "Especially" [Megalynarion], the choir chants "It is truly right" (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens" (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); "We have seen the true light" (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal. Paragraph 17 details Sunday evening Vespers (Forgiveness Vespers, opening Great Lent): at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 4 Penitential Stichira of the Tone of the week (found at the end of the Triodion); then 3 Stichira of the Triodion and 3 of the Menaion; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Prosomoion Theotokion from the Menaion. Entrance with the censer because of the Great Prokeimenon (performed at all Sunday evening Vespers of Great Lent); "Gladsome Light" (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Great Prokeimenon: "Turn not away Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble; hear me speedily. Attend unto my soul, and deliver it" (*Μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἀπὸ τοῦ παιδός σου*, Ps. 68:18–19 LXX) with its verses (see § 9 of the Protheoria). Litany of Fervent Supplication: "Let us all say with all our soul and with all our mind" (*Εἴπωμεν πάντες*) up to "For our Archbishop [Name]", and immediately the Exclamation: "For Thou art a merciful God..." At the Aposticha: the Idiomelon: "Thy grace hath shone forth, O Lord" (*Ἔλαμψεν ἡ χάρις σου, Κύριε*) twice, and the Martyrikon: "O Christ God, Who art glorified in the assembly of Thy Saints" (*Ὁ ἐνδοξαζόμενος ἐν ταῖς μνείαις τῶν Ἁγίων σου*); "Glory... Both now and ever...": "The ranks of Angels praise thee" (*Τῶν Ἀγγέλων αἱ τάξεις σε*). Then "Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" [Luke 2:29], the Trisagion Prayers, and the Dismissal Troparia: "O Theotokos Virgin, rejoice, Mary full of grace" (*Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*), "O Baptizer of Christ" (*Βαπτιστὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ*); "Glory...": "Intercede for us, O holy Apostles and all Saints" (*Ἱκετεύσατε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν*); "Both now and ever...": "Beneath thy compassion we take refuge, O Theotokos" (*Ὑπὸ τὴν σὴν εὐσπλαγχνίαν*). Then "Lord, have mercy" (40 times). Priest: "He Who is blessed, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." Reader: "O Heavenly King, strengthen the faith, establish the rulers..." Then three great prostrations with the Prayer of Saint Ephraim the Syrian, and Dismissal without "Through the prayers" (*Δι᾿ εὐχῶν*). Following the Dismissal, the Second Choir chants "All who under thy protection take refuge, O good one" (*Πάντων προστατεύεις ἀγαθή*). While this is chanted, the clergy and people venerate the hand of the Patriarch (or Hierarch, or Priest) and ask for mutual forgiveness and reconciliation; only after this reconciliation is completed is "Through the prayers of our holy Fathers..." proclaimed. Footnote 5 of the Greek edition observes that according to ancient Typika, this last hymn (*Ὑπὸ τὴν σὴν εὐσπλαγχνίαν*) is said without chant in recitativo in a quiet voice, adding as the reason that no prostration is made at it, while the preceding three are chanted; but Patriarch Gregory VI desired that this hymn also be chanted like the preceding ones. These hymns are sung at all Sunday Vespers throughout Great Lent, including Palm Sunday evening, but on the other days of Holy Week all four are recited simply without melody. This liturgical order is observed on every Sunday evening up to the Fifth Sunday of Great Lent.

Great Lent (First Week of the Fast): Paragraph 18 details the solemn opening of Matins on Clean Monday (the first day of Great Lent): The Priest enters the Holy Sanctuary, puts on the Epitrachilion, and taking the censer stands before the Holy Table. Censing cross-wise, he proclaims the initial blessing: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." The Reader recites the Trisagion Prayers, the Priest gives the Exclamation: "For Thine is the kingdom...", the Reader recites "Lord, have mercy" 12 times, and immediately the Priest proclaims: "Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and undivided Trinity..." Then the Proestos (Superior or Leader) reads the Six Psalms [Exapsalmos] in recitativo, while the faithful listen in complete silence and devout reverence. Paragraph 19 establishes the general weekday order observed on Tuesday and all subsequent weekdays of Great Lent (excluding Saturdays and Sundays): The Priest begins from outside the Sanctuary: "Blessed is our God...", "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King, Comforter..."; the Reader recites the Trisagion Prayers, "For Thine is the kingdom", "Lord, have mercy" 12 times, "Glory... Both now and ever...", "Come, let us worship" thrice, Psalm 50 [LXX], and the Midnight Office according to the Horologion. Then the Priest re-enters the Sanctuary to begin the Royal Office and Matins proper.

The rule for the Biblical Odes establishes that only those Odes possessing corresponding Triodia in the Triodion for that day are recited in full; of the remaining Odes, only the first verse and the concluding two verses with "Glory... Both now and ever..." are recited. However, the Eighth Ode (of the Three Holy Children in Babylon) and the Ninth Ode of Zacharias (the song of the Theotokos being reserved for "More honorable than the Cherubim") are chanted in their entirety every day. Thus, on Monday, the First Ode ("Let us sing unto the Lord") is recited in full; the Third, Fourth, Fifth, Sixth, and Seventh Odes are recited with opening and closing verses only; and the Eighth and Ninth Odes in full. On Tuesday, the First Ode has opening and closing verses only; the Second Ode ("Give ear, O heavens", Deut. 32 LXX) is recited in its entirety...

[^407]: Great Lent: Weekday Distribution of the Nine Biblical Odes and Order of Canons (§ 19 Continued). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p695 (printed page 680) and facing English leaf p696 (printed page 681). Weekday Matins Order: Paragraph 19 details the distribution of the Nine Biblical Odes for the remainder of the week: On Wednesday, the First Ode has opening and closing verses; the Third Ode ("My heart is established in the Lord", 1 Sam. 2 LXX) is recited in full; the Fourth, Fifth, Sixth, and Seventh Odes have opening and closing verses; and the Eighth and Ninth Odes are recited in full. On Thursday, the First and Third Odes have opening and closing verses; the Fourth Ode ("O Lord, I have heard Thy report, and was afraid", Hab. 3 LXX) is recited in full; the Fifth, Sixth, and Seventh Odes have opening and closing verses; and the Eighth and Ninth Odes in full. On Friday, the First, Third, and Fourth Odes have opening and closing verses; the Fifth Ode ("My soul yearns for Thee in the night", Isa. 26 LXX) is recited in full; on Cheesefare Friday only, the Sixth and Seventh Odes are recited in full, whereas on all other Fridays of Great Lent they have opening and closing verses only; and the Eighth and Ninth Odes are recited in full on every Friday. The rubric clarifies that by "opening verse" of an Ode is meant the scriptural verse printed at its incipit (e.g., Ode 1: "Let us sing unto the Lord, for He hath triumphed gloriously"; Ode 3: "Holy art Thou, O Lord, and my spirit praiseth Thee"; Ode 4: "Glory to Thy power, O Lord"). Order of the Canons: During Cheesefare week, the Canons of the Octoechos and Menaion precede the Triodia. Footnote 7 notes that both Canons of the Octoechos are chanted in those Odes lacking Triodia, but where Triodia exist the Second Canon is omitted; if the Triodion has two Heirmoi (e.g. Wednesday and Friday), both Octoechos Canons and the Menaion Canon are omitted. During the Forty-day Fast [Lent], the Octoechos Canons are omitted. On Monday, after the First Ode of the Menaion, follow the Triodia of the First Ode with the Verse: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". Footnote 8 notes that strictly speaking no verse is required before the Triodia since the preceding Biblical Ode supplies the verses; only the Second Ode in the Horologion assigns the verse "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee" because "Give ear, O heavens" lacks verses; nevertheless, priests have customarily prefixed "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee" before all Triodia. Then follows the Third Ode of the Menaion, the Heirmos of the First Ode of the Triodion, the Small Litany, the Sessional Hymn of the Menaion with its Theotokion, and Odes 4, 5, and 6 of the Menaion.
