Paragraph 66 Concluded: On Palm Sunday evening at the rite of Mutual Forgiveness during Compline, the Stavrotheotokion is chanted: "When the Virgin beheld Thy unjust slaughter, O Christ..." (Sphagēn sou tēn adikon); Dismissal: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee... May the Lord, coming unto His voluntary Passion for our salvation, Christ our true God..." (Erchomenos ho Kyrios epi to hekousion pathos dia tēn hēmōn sōtērian), and: "Through the prayers of our holy fathers...". Footnote 37 notes that this exact Dismissal formula is maintained throughout Passion Week until Great and Holy Wednesday at Matins and at the Divine Liturgy. Paragraph 67: Great and Holy Monday at Matins (The Service of the Bridegroom / Nymphios): After the initial blessing: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages", the Superior [Proestos] says: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter...", the Reader recites the Trisagion Prayers, the Priest gives the exclamation: "For Thine is the kingdom...", the Reader recites "Lord, have mercy" (12 times), "Glory... Both now and ever...", "O come, let us worship and fall down before our King and God..." (3 times), and the Royal Psalms: Psalm 19 LXX ("The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble...") and Psalm 20 LXX ("The king shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord..."). While these Psalms are being read slowly, the Priest censes the people with the hand-censer [katzion]. After the Trisagion Prayers and "For Thine is the kingdom...", the Troparia: "Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance...", "Glory...": "Thou Who wast voluntarily lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God...", "Both now and ever...": "O awesome and unashamed protection...". The Dean or presiding Reader [Proistamenos] recites the Six Psalms. After the Great Litany, the Great Alleluia is chanted with its appointed verses from Isaiah 26:9 LXX: "From night until morning my spirit seeketh Thee early, O God, for Thy commandments are a light upon the earth", twice in slow melody and twice in brief melody. Then the solemn Dismissal Troparion of the Bridegroom in Tone 8: "Behold, the Bridegroom cometh in the middle of the night, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watching..." (Idou ho Nymphios erchetai) three times (twice slowly and once rapidly). At the conclusion of the first time we say: "...through the protection of the Bodiless Hosts, save us!" (Prostasiais tōn Asōmatōn sōson hēmas); Footnote 38 notes that on Great Tuesday this ending is "...through the intercessions of the Forerunner, save us", and on Great Wednesday "...by the power of Thy Cross, save us". At the second time we join the commemoration of the Patron Saint of the temple: "...through the intercessions of Saint [N.] (or: the Saints), save us!"; and at the third time: "...through the Theotokos, have mercy on us!". Then the Kathismata of the Psalter: Footnote 39 records that while the daily Psalter Kathismata are commonly omitted in most parish churches during these Bridegroom Matins services either for the sake of brevity or because five Kathismata are assigned each day, they are read privately in the morning by the Priest; nevertheless it is devoutly to be wished that at least a portion of the five Kathismata be read publicly for the spiritual edification of the faithful, as the Psalter is the basis of church prayer (as noted in the Introductory Chapter [Protheoria] § 3, footnote 3). Following the Psalter, the three appointed Sessional Hymns [Kathismata] of the Triodion are chanted slowly in sequence: the first two once each, and the third twice. Immediately the Priest exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel...".

[^441]: Holy Week: Great and Holy Monday Matins Concluded (§ 67 Concluded). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p763 (printed page 748) and facing English leaf p764 (printed page 749). Paragraph 67 Concluded: The Priest reads the Matins Gospel pericope: Matthew 21:18–43 (The Cursing of the Barren Fig Tree and the Parable of the Wicked Vinedressers). After the Gospel, Psalm 50 is read plain; then the Three-Ode Canon [Triodion] of Great Monday by Saint Cosmas the Melodist (Odes 1, 8, and 9) in Tone 2 is chanted, with six Troparia in each Ode, followed by the Heirmos chanted slowly as Katavasia. After Ode 1, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 8: "Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph, while that noble man was seated in a chariot and honored as a king..." (Ho Iakōb ōdyreto), the Ikos: "Let us now add our lamentations to the lamentations of Jacob...", the Menologion from the Menaion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion on the Patriarch Joseph the All-Comely and the Withered Fig Tree. Then Ode 8 with its Heirmos; in place of "Glory...", we say: "We bless the Lord: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit", and before repeating the Heirmos as Katavasia: "We praise, we bless, and we worship the Lord". "Glory... Both now and ever...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: "O Lord, coming unto Thy Passion, Thou didst take Thy Disciples aside and comfort them...". Footnote 40 details the patriarchal ceremonial during the Praises: at the singing of "Praise ye" [Aineite], the Ecumenical Patriarch or presiding Hierarch descends from his throne to venerate the holy Icons of the Passion of Christ, blesses the people while the choirs chant "Many years to you, Master!" (Eis polla etē), and ascends the small side-throne [parathronion]. Small Doxology: "To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God..." read plain. After the litany: "Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord", the First Choir begins the Aposticha: "O Lord, the mother of the sons of Zebedee, unable to understand the ineffable mystery of Thy dispensation, requested of Thee the honor of a temporal kingdom for her sons..." with verses from Psalm 89 LXX. Then: "It is good to give praise unto the Lord...", the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: "Jacob lamented the loss of Joseph...", "Lord, have mercy" (12 times); Footnote 41 references footnote 31 regarding the liturgical usage of this response. The Priest: "Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God...", the Reader: "Confirm, O God, the holy Orthodox faith...", the Prayer: "O Heavenly King, strengthen our faithful civil authorities...", the three Great Prostrations with the Prayer of Saint Ephrem the Syrian, and the solemn Passion Week Dismissal: "May the Lord, coming unto His voluntary Passion for our salvation, Christ our true God...". Footnote 42 records that this identical order of Matins is observed on Great Tuesday and Great Wednesday, whether celebrated in the morning or in the evening as Bridegroom Matins; if celebrated in the evening, the Psalter Kathismata are postponed to the morning.

Paragraph 74 Concluded: Great Tuesday Great Compline concludes: After the Doxology: "Glory to God in the highest...", the First Choir begins the Three-Ode Canon [Triodion] of Great Tuesday evening (Odes 3, 8, and 9) in Tone 2 by Saint Cosmas the Melodist; after the Heirmos of Ode 9: "With faith let us magnify her that supernaturally conceived in the flesh..." (Tēn hyperphyōs sarki), the Trisagion Prayers, "O Lord of hosts, be with us...", and the conclusion of Great Compline. At the rite of Mutual Forgiveness, the Stavrotheotokion is chanted: "When the Virgin beheld Thy unjust slaughter, O Christ...". Paragraph 75: Great and Holy Wednesday Matins and Hours: Matins is chanted unalterably according to the rubrics of Paragraph 67. Footnote 43 records that at the Aposticha of Matins on this night, the Second Choir sings slowly and with elaborate melody the renowned Doxastikon in Tone 8: "O Lord, the woman who had fallen into many sins, having recognized Thy divinity, O Lord, taking upon herself the office of a myrrh-bearer, bringeth myrrh with lamentations unto Thee before Thy burial..." (Kyrie, hē en pollais hamartiais), universally attributed to the Nun Kassiani, though an ancient Jerusalem manuscript attributes it to Patriarch Photios. In the morning, the next five Kathismata of the Psalter are read [Kathismata 14, 15, 16, 19, and 20], thereby completing the entire Psalter (Kathisma 17 is omitted because it is reserved for Great Saturday Matins, and Kathisma 18 is omitted because it is read at every Presanctified Liturgy). The plain Hours are read as on the previous days; after the Prayer: "All-Holy Trinity...", the Dismissal is given, and Vespers begins. Paragraph 76: Great Wednesday Vespers with the Presanctified Liturgy: After Psalm 103 LXX and Kathisma 18 ("Unto the Lord"), at "Lord, I have cried", 10 verses are set, and all the Stichera sung at Matins at the Praises and Aposticha are chanted. "Glory... Both now and ever...": the Doxastikon of the Nun Kassiani: "O Lord, the woman who had fallen into many sins...". Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, "O Gladsome Light", and two Old Testament Readings: Exodus 2:11–23 LXX (Moses Slays the Egyptian and Flees to Midian) and Job 2:1–10 LXX (Job's Affliction with Sores and His Integrity). Then "Let my prayer arise", and the Gospel pericope: Matthew 26:6–16 (The Anointing of Jesus at the House of Simon the Leper and Judas Bargains to Betray Him). The Presanctified Liturgy is completed, this being the final Presanctified Liturgy of Great Lent. Paragraph 77: Great Wednesday Evening Small Compline: In the evening, Small Compline is read rather than Great Compline, marking the transition away from the Great Lenten cycle. After "It is truly meet" (Axion estin), the Three-Ode Canon [Triodion] of Great Wednesday evening in Tone 4: "A guest-room furnished and ready..." (Anōgeōn estrōmenon) is chanted with the verse: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!". After Ode 9, the Heirmos: "The childbirth of a conception without seed..." (Asporou syllēpseōs)...

[^444]: Holy Week: Great Wednesday (Compline Concluded) and Great Thursday (Matins, Vespers Opening) (§§ 77 Concluded, 78, 79 Opening). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p769 (printed page 754) and facing English leaf p770 (printed page 755). Paragraph 77 Concluded: Great Wednesday Small Compline concludes: After Ode 9 of the Triodion Canon, the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion in Tone 4: "Having transgressed more than the harlot, O Good One, I have in no wise brought forth a flood of tears for Thee; but falling down in silence before Thee, I kiss Thy most pure feet with love..." (Hyper tēn pornēn, Agathe), "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), the Prayer of the Hours: "Thou Who at all times and at every hour...", the nocturnal prayer: "O spotless, undefiled, incorrupt, unblemished, pure Virgin, Lady Bride of God..." (Aspile, amolynte), etc., and the Dismissal. Paragraph 78: Great and Holy Thursday at Matins (The Mystical Supper): After the Six Psalms and the Great Litany, the Alleluia is chanted with its verses in Tone 8 four times, followed by the renowned Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: "When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice; and to lawless judges he delivered Thee, the righteous Judge. Behold his goods, O lover of money, who for the sake thereof hanged himself! Flee from the insatiable soul that dared such things against the Master! O Lord, Who art good towards all, glory to Thee!" (Hote hoi endoxoi Mathētai) three times. Directly the Matins Gospel pericope is read: Luke 22:1–39 (The Plot of the Chief Priests, the Preparation of the Passover, the Institution of the Holy Eucharist, the Dispute about Greatness, and Christ's Agony in Gethsemane). Then Psalm 50 is read, and the acrostic Canon of Great Thursday by Saint Cosmas the Melodist in Tone 6: "The red sea was severed by the divine rod..." (Tomē tmēgetai) is chanted without biblical verses, with its Katavasia at the end of each Ode. After Ode 3, the Sessional Hymns [Kathismata]: "He Who created the lakes, the springs and the seas, desiring to teach us the highest humility, girded Himself with a towel and washed the feet of the Disciples...", "Glory...": "Having humbled Thyself through compassion, Thou didst wash the feet of Thy Disciples...", "Both now and ever...": "Eating, O Master, with Thy Disciples, Thou didst mystically reveal Thy holy slaughter...". After Ode 6, the Kontakion in Tone 2: "Having taken the Bread into his hands, the traitor extends them secretly to receive the price of Him Who fashioned man with His own hands; and Judas remained incorrigible, having dipped his hand into the dish with Christ...", the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion on the Mystical Supper, the Washing of the Disciples' Feet, the Agony in the Garden, and the Betrayal of Judas. After the Heirmos of Ode 8 is chanted as Katavasia, the Deacon exclaims: "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!", and Ode 9 is chanted with its Heirmos: "Come, O believers, let us enjoy the hospitality and immortal table of the Master in the upper chamber..." (Xenias Despotikēs). Exaposteilarion: "I see Thy bridal chamber adorned, O my Savior..." three times. At the Praises [Lauds], four Stichera are chanted: "The assembly of the Jews hastens together to deliver the Creator and Fashioner of all unto Pilate...", "Judas the transgressor, having dipped his hand into the dish with Thee at supper...", "Judas, being a treacherous servant, deceitfully devised betrayal...", and "Judas, servant and deceiver, disciple and plotter, friend and devil, was made manifest from his deeds...". "Glory... Both now and ever...": Doxastikon in Tone 2: "The Lamb whom Isaiah proclaimed comes of His own will to the slaughter..." (Hon ekēryxen Amnon). The Small Doxology: "To Thee belongs glory, O Lord our God..." read plain. The litany: "Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord", and the four Aposticha with verses from Psalm 40 LXX: "Today the evil Sanhedrin has assembled together against Christ..." with verse: "He that eats of my bread has lifted up his heel against me" (Ps. 40:9 LXX); "Today Judas hides his treachery under the pretense of love for the poor..." with verse: "When he went abroad, he spoke of the same" (Ps. 40:6 LXX); "Thy deceitful manner is revealed unto the end..." with verse: "An evil word have they poured out against me" (Ps. 40:8 LXX); and "O believers, let none of us who are uninitiated draw near to the Master's table...". "Glory...": "Thy deceitful manner..."; "Both now and ever...": "Initiating Thy Disciples, O Lord, Thou didst teach them, saying: O my friends, see that no fear separate you from Me...". Then: "It is good to give praise unto the Lord...", the Trisagion Prayers, the Troparion of the Prophecy: "Thou Who didst endure slaps for the human race, O Christ God, deliver us from corruption and save our souls", and the Old Testament Prophecy: Jeremiah 11:18–12:5, 9–11, 14–15 LXX (The Prophecy of the Innocent Lamb Led to the Slaughter). The Augmented Litany [Ektenis], and the Dismissal. Paragraph 79: Great Thursday Vespers with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great: At Vespers, after Psalm 103 LXX, at "Lord, I have cried", five Idiomela of the Praises are chanted, repeating the first one for six. "Glory... Both now and ever...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: "Judas is truly the offspring of vipers, who ate the manna in the wilderness and murmured against the Nourisher..." (Gennēma echidnōn). Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel, "O Gladsome Light", and Old Testament Readings from Exodus 19:10–19 LXX, Job...

[^445]: Great and Holy Thursday: Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great Concluded and Service of the Holy Passions Opening (§§ 79 Concluded, 80 Opening). Paragraph 79 Concluded: Great Thursday Vespers with the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great concludes: Following the Old Testament readings (Exodus 19:10–19 LXX, Job 38:1–21; 42:1–5 LXX, and Isaiah 50:4–11 LXX), the Small Litany is proclaimed, the Trisagion Hymn is chanted, and the Epistle (1 Corinthians 11:23–32: The Institution of the Holy Eucharist) and composite Passion Gospel (Matthew 26:2–20; John 13:3–17; Matthew 26:21–39; Luke 22:43–45; Matthew 26:40–27:2: The Composite Passion Gospel of the Mystical Supper) are proclaimed. Throughout this Liturgy, in place of the Cherubic Hymn, the Communion Hymn, and "We have seen the true light", the Troparion in Tone 6 is chanted: "Of Thy Mystical Supper, O Son of God, receive me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of the Mystery to Thine enemies, neither will I give Thee a kiss as did Judas, but like the thief do I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!" (Tou deipnou sou tou mystikou). After "Blessed be the name of the Lord...", the solemn Passion Dismissal is given: "Glory to Thee, our God, our hope, glory to Thee. May He Who out of exceeding goodness showed humility to be the most excellent way when He washed the feet of the Disciples, and condescended unto the Cross and burial for our sake, Christ our true God...", and "Through the prayers of our holy fathers...". Footnote 44 directs the reader to Appendix [Parartima] IV for the extensive ceremonial rubrics of the Service of the Holy Passions as celebrated in the Patriarchate of Constantinople. Paragraph 80: Great and Holy Thursday Evening (The Service of the Twelve Gospels of the Holy Passions): In the evening at the First Hour of the night (7:00 p.m.), the Priest gives the initial blessing, the Superior [Proestos] says "Glory to Thee, our God...", "O Heavenly King", the Reader recites the Trisagion Prayers, the Priest "For Thine is the kingdom...", the Reader "Lord, have mercy" (12 times), "Glory... Both now and ever...", "O come, let us worship" (3 times), and the Royal Psalms: Psalm 19 LXX ("The Lord hear Thee in the day of trouble...") and Psalm 20 LXX ("The king shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord..."). While these are read slowly, the Priest censes the temple and people with the hand-censer [katzion]. Trisagion Prayers, Troparia ("Save, O Lord, Thy people..."), and the Superior recites the Six Psalms. After the Great Litany, the brief Alleluia is chanted four times with its verses in Tone 8, followed by the Dismissal Troparion of Great Thursday in Tone 8: "When the glorious Disciples were enlightened at the Supper during the washing of the feet, then the ungodly Judas was darkened by the disease of avarice..." (Hote hoi endoxoi mathētai) twice slowly and once rapidly. The Archbishop or presiding Priest proclaims the First Gospel of the Testament (John 13:31–18:1: The Farewell Discourse of Christ to His Disciples). At the conclusion, the Archbishop blesses the congregation with the three-stemmed candlestick [trikirion] while the choirs sing "Many years to you, Master!" (Eis polla etē), and ascends the episcopal throne. The choirs then alternate in chanting the Antiphons, beginning with Antiphon 1 in Tone 8: "The rulers of the peoples took counsel together against the Lord and against His Anointed" (Archontes laōn) through Antiphon 3, concluding with the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 7: "Sustaining the disciples at the supper, Thou didst say: One of you will betray Me..." (En tō deipnō tous mathētas).

[^446]: Great and Holy Thursday Evening: Service of the Holy Passions Continued (Gospels II–IX, Antiphons IV–XV, Procession of the Holy Cross, Beatitudes, and Canon) (§ 80 Continued). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p773 (printed page 758) and facing English leaf p774 (printed page 759). Paragraph 80 Continued: The Second Gospel is proclaimed: John 18:1–28 (Jesus in Gethsemane, His Arrest, Interrogation before Annas, and Peter's Denial). At its conclusion, the Second Choir sings the universal Passion response: "Glory to Thy forbearance, O Lord, glory to Thee!" (Doxa tē makrothymia sou Kyrie doxa soi), which is repeated after every subsequent Gospel reading throughout the service. The Fourth Antiphon in Tone 5 is begun, continuing through Antiphons 5 and 6, concluding with the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 7: "What reason has made thee, O Judas, a traitor of the Savior? Did He cast thee off from the choir of the Apostles? Did He deprive thee of the gift of healings?..." (Poios se tropos Iouda). The Third Gospel is proclaimed: Matthew 26:57–75 (Jesus before Caiaphas, the False Witnesses, the Sanhedrin's Condemnation, and Peter Weeps Bitterly). The choirs chant Antiphons 7, 8, and 9, concluding with the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 8: "O how did Judas, who was once Thy disciple, devise betrayal against Thee?..." (Ō pōs Ioudas ho pote sou mathētēs). The Fourth Gospel is proclaimed: John 18:28–19:16 (Jesus before Pilate, the Crowning with Thorns, the Scourging, Ecce Homo, and the Sentence of Crucifixion). Antiphons 10, 11, and 12 are chanted, concluding with the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 8: "When Thou, O God, didst stand before Caiaphas, and wast delivered unto Pilate, the Judge of all: the powers of heaven shook with fear..." (Hote parestēs tō Kaiapha ho Theos). The Fifth Gospel is proclaimed: Matthew 27:3–32 (The Remorse and Death of Judas, Jesus before Pilate, Barabbas, and Simon of Cyrene Bears the Cross). The First Choir begins Antiphon 13 in Tone 6, followed by Antiphon 14. At the Fifteenth Antiphon, the solemn rite of the Procession of the Holy Cross (exodos tou Stavrou) is enacted according to universal Greek usage: the Priest, vested in phelonion and carrying the large carved wooden Crucifix upon his shoulder, preceded by processional fans [rhipidia], candles, and the hand-censer, exits the Sanctuary through the northern door and processes around the nave of the temple, chanting in a solemn recitative intonation: "Today is hung upon the Tree, He Who suspended the earth upon the waters..." (Sēmeron krematai epi xylou) three times, the choir repeating the verse after him while the faithful kneel in adoration; the Crucifix is then planted firmly in the center of the temple on the Tetrapod. The Antiphons conclude with the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 4: "Thou hast ransomed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood..." (Exēgorasas hēmas). The Sixth Gospel is proclaimed: Mark 15:16–32 (The Crucifixion at Golgotha and the Mocking by the Rulers). The First Choir chants the Beatitudes [Makarismoi] interspersed with Passion Troparia, followed by the Prokimenon in Tone 4 chanted three times: "They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots" (Ps. 21:18 LXX / Diemarisanto ta himatia mou heautois). The Seventh Gospel is proclaimed: Matthew 27:33–54 (The Crucifixion, the Darkness, the Rending of the Temple Veil, the Resuscitation of the Saints, and the Centurion's Confession). Psalm 50 LXX is recited plain, followed immediately by the Eighth Gospel: Luke 23:32–49 (The Good Thief and the Repentant Confession: "Remember me, Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom"). The First Choir begins the solemn Triodion Canon of Great Friday in Tone 6 by Saint Cosmas the Melodist: "Early in the morning my soul rises unto Thee, O Word of God..." (Pros se orthrizō), with four Troparia for each Ode without biblical verses, the Heirmos being repeated slowly at the end of each Ode as Katavasia. After Ode 5, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 8: "Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us; for Mary beheld Him upon the Tree and said: Even though Thou dost endure the Cross, Thou art my Son and my God!" (Ton di' hēmas stavrōthenta), the Ikos, the Menologion, and the Memorial [Hypomnema] of the Triodion on the Holy and Salvific Passions. Ode 9 is chanted with the exclamation "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!", followed by the Small Litany and the solemn Exaposteilarion in Tone 3: "The wise thief in a single hour Thou didst account worthy of Paradise, O Lord; enlighten me also by the wood of the Cross, and save me!" (Ton lēstēn authēmeron) three times. The Ninth Gospel is proclaimed: John 19:25–37 (Christ Entrusts His Mother to the Beloved Disciple, "It Is Finished", and the Piercing of His Sacred Side). At the Praises [Lauds], three Idiomela are chanted with four verses from Psalm 150 LXX, repeating the first: "Two evil deeds has My first-born son Israel committed..." (Ps. 150:2 LXX) and "Every member of Thy holy flesh endured dishonor for our sake..." (Ps. 150:4 LXX).

Paragraph 80 Concluded: The service of the Holy Passions concludes: At the Praises, after the fourth verse from Psalm 150:5–6 LXX ("Praise Him with sounding cymbals..."), the third Idiomelon is chanted: "Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, all creation trembled..." The Deacon intones the Augmented Litany: "Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy...", commemorating the hierarchical authorities and all Orthodox Christians. After the exclamation "For Thou art a merciful and loving God...", the Deacon proclaims "Wisdom!", the Priest "Blessed is He Who is, Christ our God...", and the Archbishop or Superior recites the prayer of confirmation: "Confirm, O Lord God, the holy Orthodox faith of pious and Orthodox Christians unto ages of ages" (Stereōsai Kyrios ho Theos). The Priest pronounces the solemn Passion Dismissal: "Glory to Thee, O God, our hope, glory to Thee. May Christ our true God, Who endured spittings, and scourgings, buffetings, and the Cross and Death for the salvation of the world, through the intercessions of His all-pure and blameless holy Mother, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind" (Doxa soi ho Theos hē elpis hēmōn doxa soi; ho emptysmous kai mastigas...), and the final benediction: "Through the prayers of our holy fathers...".

Paragraph 81: Great and Holy Friday Morning: The Royal Hours (First, Third, Sixth, and Ninth): At the First Hour of the day (around 7:00 a.m.), the Priest gives the initial blessing: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages", the Superior [Proestos] recites "O Heavenly King", the Reader the Trisagion Prayers, the Priest "For Thine is the kingdom...", the Reader "Lord, have mercy" (12 times), "Glory... (Ton di' hēmas stavrōthenta), "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), the Prayer of the Hours: "Thou Who at all times and at every hour...", and the Superior says the prayer of Saint Basil the Great: "O Christ, the True Light, Who enlightenest and sanctifiest every man that cometh into the world..." (Christe to phōs). Footnote 45 notes that during this Hour, as well as during the Third and Sixth Hours, one of the deacons according to their order of seniority, vested in his customary monastic mandya, censes the temple with the hand-censer [katzion]. The Third Hour follows immediately: Beginning with the Trisagion Prayers, the three Psalms of the Third Hour are read: Psalm 34 LXX ("Judge Thou, O Lord, them that injure me..."), Psalm 108 LXX ("O God, pass not over my praise in silence..."), and Psalm 50 LXX ("Have mercy on me, O God..."). "Glory...": Troparion in Tone 6: "O Lord, the Jews condemned Thee to death, the Life of all..." (Kyrie, katekrinan se Ioudaioi thanatō); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: "O Theotokos, thou art the true vine that blossomed for us the fruit of life...". The Second Choir chants the first Idiomelon in Tone 6: "Through fear of the Jews, Peter Thy friend and companion denied Thee, O Lord..." (Dia ton phobon tōn Ioudaiōn); the First Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 6: "Before Thy precious Cross, when the soldiers mocked Thee, O Lord, the angelic hosts were struck with dread..." (Pro tou timiou sou Stavrou) with verse from Psalm 5:1 LXX ("Give ear to my words, O Lord; understand my cry"); the Second Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": "Drawn upon the Cross, Thou didst cry aloud, O Lord: For which deed do the Jews wish to stone Me? Because I healed their paralytics?..." (Helkomenos epi Stavrou). The Old Testament Prophecy: Isaiah 50:4–11 LXX (The Suffering Servant: "I gave my back to scourges, and my cheeks to blows"); the Epistle: Romans 5:6–10 (While We Were Still Helpless, Christ Died for the Ungodly); and the Gospel: Mark 15:16–41 (The Soldiers Mock Christ in the Praetorium, the Crucifixion at the Third Hour, the Inscription of the Accusation, and the Death of Christ). The Reader: "Blessed is the Lord God, blessed is the Lord day by day...", the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: "Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us...", "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), "Thou Who at all times...", the Prayer of Saint Mardarios: "O Master God, Father Almighty, Lord, Only-Begotten Son Jesus Christ, and Holy Spirit, one Divinity, one Power, have mercy on me a sinner...", and the Sixth Hour begins.

Paragraph 82: The Royal Sixth Hour: Celebrated with the three appointed Psalms: Psalm 53 LXX ("Save me, O God, by Thy name..."), Psalm 139 LXX ("Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man..."), and Psalm 90 LXX ("He that dwelleth in the help of the Most High..."). "Glory...": Troparion in Tone 2: "Thou hast worked salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God; Thou didst stretch out Thy most pure hands upon the Cross; Thou didst gather all the nations that cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord, glory to Thee!" (Eirgasō sōtērian en mesō tēs gēs); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: "Seeing that we have no boldness because of our manifold sins...". The First Choir chants the first Idiomelon in Tone 8: "Thus saith the Lord unto the Jews: My people, what have I done unto you, or wherein have I grieved you? Your blind have I given sight, your lepers have I cleansed, the man lying on his pallet have I restored. My people, what have I done unto you, and wherewith have you repaid Me? Instead of manna, gall; instead of water, vinegar; instead of loving Me, you have nailed Me to the Cross!..." (Tade legei Kyrios pros Ioudaious); the Second Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 8: "O lawgivers of Israel, Jews and Pharisees, the choir of the Apostles cries aloud unto you: Behold the Temple which you destroyed; behold the Lamb Whom you crucified and delivered unto the tomb!..." (Hoi nomothetai Israēl) with verse from Psalm 68:21 LXX ("They gave Me gall for My food, and for My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink"); the First Choir chants "Glory... Both now and ever...": "Come, O Christ-bearing peoples, let us behold what counsel Judas the traitor took with the lawless priests against our Savior..." (Deute christophoroi laoi). The Old Testament Prophecy: Isaiah 52:13–54:1 LXX (The Fourth Servant Song: "He was wounded for our iniquities, and bruised for our transgressions; the chastisement of our peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed"); the Epistle: Hebrews 2:11–18 (Christ Partook of Flesh and Blood that through Death He Might Destroy the Devil); and the Gospel: Luke 23:32–49 (The Crucifixion between Two Malefactors, "Father, forgive them", the Good Thief Confesses Christ, the Sun Darkened at the Sixth Hour, and Jesus Cries with a Loud Voice and Breathes His Last). The Reader recites: "Let Thy tender mercies speedily prevent us, O Lord, for we are brought very low..." (Ps. 78:8 LXX), the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: "Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us...", "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), "Thou Who at all times...", the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great: "O God and Lord of powers, and Maker of all creation, Who through the compassion of Thine inscrutable mercy didst send down Thine Only-Begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, for the salvation of our race...", and the Ninth Hour begins. Paragraph 83: The Royal Ninth Hour: Celebrated with the three appointed Psalms: Psalm 68 LXX ("Save me, O God, for the waters are come in even unto my soul..."), Psalm 69 LXX ("O God, draw nigh unto my help; Lord, make haste to help me..."), and Psalm 85 LXX ("Bow down Thine ear, O Lord, and hear me, for I am poor and needy..."). "Glory...": Troparion in Tone 8: "When the thief beheld the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, he said: If Thou wert not God incarnate Who art crucified with us, the sun would not have hidden its rays, nor would the earth have shaken with trembling. But O Thou Who endurest all things, remember me, O Lord, in Thy kingdom!" (Horōn ho lēstēs ton archēgon tēs zōēs); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion: "O Good One, Who for our sake wast born of a Virgin and didst endure crucifixion, Who by death didst despoil death and didst manifest the Resurrection as God...". The Second Choir chants the first Idiomelon in Tone 7: "A marvelous and fearful wonder it was to behold today: the Creator of heaven and earth hangs upon the Tree; He Who suspended the earth upon the waters is transfixed with nails; the sun hides its rays at the sight of the Master dishonored..." (Thambos ēn katidein ton ouranou kai gēs Poiētēn); the First Choir chants the second Idiomelon in Tone 2: "When the transgressors nailed the Lord of glory upon the Cross, they mocked Him and said: If Thou art the Son of God, save Thyself and come down from the Cross!..." (Hote se stavrō prosēlōsan paranomoi) with verse from Psalm 21:18 LXX ("They divided My garments among them, and for My vesture did they cast lots"); the Second Choir takes up the conclusion: "...Together with the Father and the Holy Spirit!"; the First Choir chants "Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit"; the Second Choir chants "Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.". At this point, the Canonarch advances to the center of the temple before the Holy Cross and intones in the solemn recitative manner of the Epistle the renowned Idiomelon: "Today is hung upon the Tree, He Who suspended the earth upon the waters..." (Sēmeron krematai epi xylou) three times, along with its verses: "A crown of thorns crowns Him Who is the King of angels. He is wrapped in false purple, Who wrapped the heavens with clouds. He received buffetings, Who freed Adam in the Jordan. He was transfixed with nails, Who is the Bridegroom of the Church. He was pierced with a spear, Who is the Son of the Virgin. We worship Thy Passion, O Christ! (3 times). Show us also Thy glorious Resurrection!", after which the same Sticheron is chanted antiphonaally by both choirs verse by verse. The Old Testament Prophecy: Jeremiah 11:18–12:5, 9–11, 14–15 LXX (The Innocent Lamb Led to the Slaughter: "I was like an innocent lamb led to the slaughter; I knew not that they devised an evil device against me"); the Epistle: Hebrews 10:19–31 (Having Boldness to Enter into the Holiest by the Blood of Jesus, by a New and Living Way Which He Dedicated for Us through the Veil, that is to say, His Flesh); and the Gospel: John 19:23–37 (The Soldiers Part His Garments, Jesus Commends His Mother to the Beloved Disciple, He Receives the Vinegar and Gives Up the Ghost, the Soldiers Break Not His Legs, and One Pierces His Side with a Spear). The Reader recites the Trisagion Prayers, the Kontakion: "Come, let us all hymn Him Who was crucified for us...", "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), "Thou Who at all times...", the Prayer of Saint Basil the Great: "O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who hast patiently endured our transgressions, and hast brought us even unto this present hour, in which, hanging upon the life-creating Tree, Thou didst open the way into Paradise unto the penitent thief, and by death didst destroy death...", and the Dismissal is given, concluding the solemn Royal Hours of Great and Holy Friday.

Six priests with uncovered heads (without kamilavkia), vested in phelonia and epitrachilia, carrying the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] upon their heads with reverence, led by the Great Archimandrite carrying the Holy Gospel Book, exit from the Sanctuary preceded by candle-bearers, processional fans [hexapteryga], the chanters, the Primikirios bearing the two-branched candlestick [divamvoulon], and deacons censing; they advance to the middle of the nave, where the decorated Tomb [Kuvuklion] stands prepared.

Paragraph 84 Concluded: The solemn procession of the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] reaches the center of the temple where the Tomb [Sepulchre / Kuvuklion] stands decorated. Paragraph 85 Opening / Footnote 46: Great and Holy Saturday Matins (The Service of the Lamentations / Epitaphios Threnos): Heading and historical-canonical footnote. Footnote 46 records that because many faithful in urban settings experienced difficulty leaving their homes around midnight to attend the Matins service at the Seventh Hour of the night (1:00 a.m.), pastoral economy and dispensation [oikonomia] established the custom of anticipating this Matins service to the First Hour of the night (7:00 p.m. on Friday evening), coinciding with the traditional hour of the Bridegroom Matins services earlier in Holy Week. The Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great is postponed until the following morning (Holy Saturday); thus the immense length of a combined nocturnal vigil is divided into two manageable liturgical celebrations.

Paragraph 85 Opening: Great and Holy Saturday Matins (The Lamentations at the Tomb / Epitaphios Threnos): When celebrated according to ancient monastic observance at the Seventh Hour of the night (1:00 a.m.), the Amomos (Psalm 118 LXX) and the Old Testament readings omitted from the Vespers of Great Saturday are read here (Footnote 47 notes that if Matins is anticipated at 7:00 p.m., the Amomos and readings are read in the morning before Vespers). The Priest gives the blessing: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages"; the Superior [Proestos] says: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King...", the Reader the Trisagion Prayers, the Priest "For Thine is the kingdom...", the Reader the Troparia ("Save, O Lord, Thy people..."), and the Superior recites the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord" (Theos Kyrios), the Dismissal Troparia in Tone 2: "The noble Joseph..." until "and laid It for burial"; "Glory...": Tone 2: "When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brilliance of Thy Divinity..." (Hote katelthes pros ton thanaton) in its entirety; "Both now and ever...": Tone 2: "Unto the myrrh-bearing women..." until "foreign to corruption". Small Litany, followed by the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 1: "In a clean shroud and with spices, the noble Joseph, taking down Thine all-pure Body from the Tree, wrapped It and laid It in a new tomb; and so early in the morning the myrrh-bearing women cried aloud: Show us, O Christ, Thy Resurrection!" (Sindoni kathara) once, slowly; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 1: "The angelic choirs were astounded at the sight of Him Who rests in the bosom of the Father being laid in a tomb as a mortal..." (Exestesan choroi) likewise slowly. Footnote 48 notes that during this hymn the Great Archdeacon and deacons receive the blessing for the time [kairos], enter the Sanctuary, vest in their sacred vestments, and emerge holding the two-branched and three-branched candlesticks [dikirotrikira]. Psalm 50 LXX, followed by the monumental Canon of Great Saturday in Tone 6: "Of old the surge of the sea covered the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves; but the children of those who were saved bury beneath the earth Him Who was hidden: let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!" (Kymati thalasses) by Mark the Monk and Saint Cosmas the Melodist for six Troparia, the Heirmos being repeated slowly at the end of each Ode as Katavasia. After Ode 3, the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] in Tone 1: "Thy tomb, O Savior, the soldiers guarding became as dead men..." (Ton taphon sou Soter) once, slowly; Footnote 49 notes that at Ode 4 the Patriarch enters the Sanctuary and vests in complete hierarchical vestments with the concelebrating Hierarchs. After Ode 6, the Small Litany, the Kontakion in Tone 2: "He Who closed the abyss is beheld dead, and wrapped in fine linen and myrrh, the Immortal One is laid in a tomb as a mortal; and the women came to anoint Him with myrrh, weeping bitterly and crying aloud: This Sabbath is most blessed, in which Christ, having fallen asleep, shall rise again on the third day!" (Ten abysson ho kleisas); the Ikos; the Menologion; and the Triodion Memorial on the bodily burial of the Lord and His descent into Hades. Odes 7 and 8 of the Canon follow. The Deacon exclaims: "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!", and Ode 9 is chanted ("Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding in the tomb the Son Whom without seed thou didst conceive in thy womb..."). At the conclusion of Ode 9, the Patriarch in full hierarchical vestments emerges from the Sanctuary preceded by the concelebrating Hierarchs; chanting the opening verse of the First Stasis of the Lamentations [Enkomia]: "Life in the tomb art Thou laid, O Christ, and the angelic hosts were astounded, glorifying Thy condescension" (He zoe en tapho), he advances toward the Epitaphios and censes it cross-wise, and afterward censes all the people. The Hierarchs, standing in choir formation, chant the verses of the First Stasis until the Patriarch returns to the throne; the opening Troparion is repeated. Small Litany with exclamation by the Patriarch: "For blessed is Thy Name, and glorified is Thy kingdom: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", and he begins the Second Stasis.

Paragraph 85 Continued: Great and Holy Saturday Matins: The Second Stasis of the Lamentations is chanted by the Patriarch and concelebrating Hierarchs: "It is right to magnify Thee, the Giver of life, Who wast lifted up upon the Cross and didst shatter the power of the enemy" (Axion esti megalynein se ton Zoodoten); at its conclusion, the first Troparion of this Stasis is repeated. The Small Litany follows, with the exclamation by the Patriarch: "For Holy art Thou, O our God, Who sittest upon the throne of glory of the Cherubim, and unto Thee we send up glory: together with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most holy, good, and life-giving Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.". The Patriarch and Hierarchs begin chanting the Third Stasis: "All generations offer a hymn unto Thy burial, O my Christ" (Hai geneai pasai hymnon te taphe sou prospherousi Christe mou). At the verse: "The myrrh-bearing women came early in the morning and sprinkled myrrh upon Thy tomb" (Erranan ton taphon hai Myrophoroi myra, lian proi elthousai), the Patriarch descends from the throne, receives a sprinkling vessel [kanion] from the Ecclesiarch, and singing this same Troparion (which is repeated three times), sprinkles the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] and the Tomb with rose-water [rhodostagma]. Upon the completion of the Third Stasis, its opening Troparion is repeated. The Small Litany follows, with the exclamation by the Patriarch: "For Thou art the King of peace, and the Savior of our souls, O Christ our God, and unto Thee we send up glory: together with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thine All-Holy, Good, and Life-giving Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.". The Patriarch and concelebrating Hierarchs immediately begin chanting the Evlogitaria of the Resurrection in Tone 5: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord: teach me Thy statutes! The assembly of the angels was amazed, beholding Thee numbered among the dead, yet destroying the power of death, O Savior, and with Thyself raising up Adam, and freeing all from Hades!..." (Eulogetos ei, Kyrie... Ton Angelon ho demos kateplage). When the Evlogitaria are completed, the Small Litany follows, with the exclamation by the Patriarch: "For all the powers of heaven praise Thee, and unto Thee they send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.". Directly the Exaposteilarion in Tone 2 is chanted: "Holy is the Lord our God" (Hagios Kyrios ho Theos hemon) three times without additional Psalm verses. "Let every breath praise the Lord" (Psalm 150:6 LXX) and the Praises [Lauds] begin. Footnote 50 (noting Violakis's errant repetition of numeral 49) records the ceremonial action during the Praises: at the verse "Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His hosts! To Thee, O God, is due a hymn!", the Patriarch descends from the throne, venerates the Epitaphios, blesses the congregation, and returns to the throne; while the remaining verses of the Praises are chanted, the concelebrating Hierarchs advance two by two, venerate the Epitaphios, and return to their stalls.

[^454]: Great and Holy Saturday: Matins Concluded (Praises Concluded, Solemn Epitaphios Procession, Prophecy, Epistle, Gospel, and Dismissal) (§ 85 Concluded). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p789 (printed page 774) and facing English leaf p790 (printed page 775). Paragraph 85 Concluded: The service of Great Saturday Matins concludes: At the Praises, four Stichera Idiomela are chanted: 1. "Today the tomb holds Him Who holds creation in the palm of His hand; a stone covers Him Who covered the heavens with virtue; Life sleeps and Hades trembles, and Adam is loosed from his bonds..." (Semeron synechei taphos); 2. "What is this sight that we behold? What is this present rest? The King of the ages, having accomplished the dispensation through His Passion, keeps Sabbath in the tomb..." (Ti to horomenon theama); 3. "Come, let us behold our Life lying in the tomb, that He may give life unto those lying in the tombs..." (Deute idomen ten zoen hemon); 4. "Joseph asked for the Body of Jesus, and laid It in his own new tomb; for it was fitting that He should come forth from a tomb as from a bridal chamber..." (Etesato Joseph to soma tou Iesou). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 2: "This present day Moses mystically prefigured, saying: And God blessed the seventh day; for this is the blessed Sabbath, this is the day of rest, whereon the Only-Begotten Son of God rested from all His works..." (Ten semeron mystikos ho megas Moyses prodietypouto legon); "Both now and ever...": Theotokion in Tone 2: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos, for through Him Who became incarnate of thee, Hades is bound, Adam is recalled, the curse is annulled, Eve is set free, death is put to death, and we are given life..." (Hypereulogemene hyparcheis). The Great Doxology is chanted; at its conclusion, the slow melismatic Asmatikon: "Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us" (Hagios ho Theos) is sung by the choirs as the solemn Procession of the Epitaphios [Plashchanytsia] departs. Order of procession: the priests lead the way, followed by the chanters, and after them the Patriarch and concelebrating Hierarchs bearing the Epitaphios upon their heads; the procession exits through the western doors of the church and circles around the perimeter before returning. Upon re-entering the temple, the Patriarch enters the Sanctuary and proclaims: "Let us attend! Peace be unto all! Wisdom!". He chants the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 2: "When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal...", censing around the Holy Table processing before the Epitaphios; then the Troparia: "Unto the myrrh-bearing women..." and "The noble Joseph..."; the priests then reverently lay the Epitaphios upon the Holy Altar Table (Footnote 51* notes that ancient Typika prescribed only "The noble Joseph", while later custom prefixed the two Resurrectional Troparia). The Reader outside the iconostasis recites the Troparion of the Prophecy in Tone 2: "O Christ, Who holdest fast the ends of the earth, Thou didst deign to be held fast in a narrow tomb, that Thou mightest deliver mankind from the fall of Hades, and raising us up, immortalize us as the immortal God!" (Ho synechon ta perata); the Prokimenon in Tone 4: "Arise, O Lord, help us, and redeem us for Thy Name's sake!" (Ps. 43:26 LXX); the Prophecy: Ezekiel 37:1–14 LXX (The Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones: "Thus saith the Lord God: Behold, I will open your graves, O My people, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel"); the Epistle: 1 Corinthians 5:6–8 and Galatians 3:13–14 (Purging out the Old Leaven, Christ Our Passover Sacrificed for Us, and Redemption from the Curse of the Law); and the Gospel: Matthew 27:62–66 (The Chief Priests and Pharisees Seal the Sepulchre and Set the Guard) read by the Patriarch before the Royal Doors. After "Many years to you, Master!" (Eis polla ete), the Patriarch unvests from his hierarchical vestments (Footnote 52* notes that if Matins was anticipated at 7:00 p.m., the Patriarch does not unvest, but remains in the Sanctuary until the end to pronounce the Dismissal of the section), puts on his monastic mandya, takes his pastoral staff, and ascends the throne. The Archdeacon recites the Augmented Litany ("Let us all say with our whole soul...") and the Morning Litany ("Let us complete our morning prayer unto the Lord"). The Priest exclaims: "For Thine it is to show mercy and to save us, O Christ our God, and unto Thee we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", and gives the Dismissal: "May Christ, our true God, Who for us men and for our salvation voluntarily endured His terrible Passions, the Cross, and voluntary entombment in the flesh, through the intercessions of His all-pure and blameless holy Mother, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind", followed by "Through the prayers of our holy fathers...".
