(Eulogemene he basileia tou Patros); and the Patriarch recites the Introductory Psalm [Psalm 103 LXX: "Bless the Lord, O my soul..."] plainly. At "Lord, I have cried" (Kyrie ekekraxa), eight stichoi are set, and the choirs chant four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1 and four Idiomela of the day in Tone 8: 1. Tone 1: "Accept our evening prayers, O holy Lord, and grant us remission of sins, for Thou alone art He Who hast manifested the Resurrection unto the world" (Tas hesperinas hemon euchas); 2. Tone 1: "Surround Zion, O ye peoples, and encompass her, and give glory within her unto Him Who is risen from the dead; for He is our God, Who hath delivered us from our iniquities" (Kyklosate laoi Sion); 3. Tone 1: "Come, ye peoples, let us hymn and worship Christ, glorifying His Resurrection from the dead; for He is our God, Who hath delivered the world from the error of the enemy" (Deute laoi hymnesomen); 4. Tone 1: "By Thy Passion, O Christ, we have been set free from passions, and by Thy Resurrection we have been delivered from corruption: O Lord, glory to Thee!" (To pathei sou Christe); 5. & 6. Tone 8: "Today Hades groaning cries aloud: Woe is me, if only I had not received Him Who was born of Mary; for coming upon me He has dissolved my power, and broken the gates of bronze; as God, He has raised up the souls that I held fast of old! Glory to Thy Cross and Thy Resurrection, O Lord!" (Semeron ho hades stenon boa) (twice); 7. Tone 8: "Today Hades groaning cries aloud: My power is dissolved; I received a dead Man as one of the dead, but could not hold Him at all, for with Him I lose those over whom I had ruled; all those whom I held fast for ages I have vomited forth! But He Who was crucified has raised up the dead! Glory to Thy Cross and Thy Resurrection, O Lord!" (Semeron ho hades stenon boa: Katelythe mou he exousia); 8. Tone 8: "Today Hades groaning cries aloud: My dominion is swallowed up; the Shepherd has been crucified, and has raised up Adam; those over whom I reigned are taken from me; whom I swallowed down in my might, I have surrendered utterly; the Crucified One has emptied the graves; the might of death has no power! Glory to Thy Cross and Thy Resurrection, O Lord!" (Semeron ho hades stenon boa: Katepothe mou to kratos). "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 6: "Moses the great mystically prefigured this present day, saying: And God blessed the seventh day; for this is the blessed Sabbath, this is the day of rest, whereon the Only-Begotten Son of God rested from all His works..." (Ten semeron mystikos ho megas Moyses); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 1: "Let us praise the Virgin Mary, the glory of the whole world, who sprang forth from mankind and gave birth to the Master, the gate of heaven..." (Ten pankosmion doxan). The Entrance is made with the Holy Gospel Book; "O Gladsome Light" (Phos hilaron) is chanted; there is no Prokimenon, but directly the three Old Testament Readings are proclaimed: 1. Genesis 1:1–13 LXX (The Creation of the World: Heaven and Earth, the Light, the Firmament, the Earth, the Seas, and Plant Life); 2. Jonah 1:1–4:11 LXX (The Entire Book of the Prophet Jonah: The Three Days and Three Nights Prefiguring the Burial and Resurrection of the Lord); 3. Daniel 3:1–23 LXX (The Three Holy Youths in the Babylonian Furnace of Fire), followed by the Prayer of Azariah [Daniel 3:26–45 LXX / Apocrypha]: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy Name unto the ages...", and the Hymn of the Three Youths [Daniel 3:52–90 LXX / Song of the Three Holy Children] through verse 56: "Blessed art Thou in the firmament of heaven, and praised and glorified unto the ages" (Eulogemenos ei en to stereomati tou ouranou). At this point, all stand and begin chanting in Tone 1 the remainder of the Hymn of the Three Youths [from verse 57]: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn and exalt Him above all forever!" (Ton Kyrion hymneite kai hyperypsoute eis pantas tous aionas), with the Canonarch intoning the intermittent verses through verse 88: "Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael; hymn and exalt Him above all forever!", the choir repeating after each verse the refrain: "Hymn and exalt Him above all forever!" (Hyperypsoute eis pantas tous aionas), concluding with the verses for the Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs, and the final Doxology: "We bless the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit: the Lord!" (Eulogoumen Patera, Yion kai Hagion Pneuma, ton Kyrion).

[^456]: Great and Holy Saturday: Vespers with the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great Continued (§ 86 Continued). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p793 (printed page 778) and facing English leaf p794 (printed page 779). Concluding cadences of the Hymn of the Three Youths: "We hymn, we bless, and we worship the Lord! Hymn and exalt Him above all forever!". The Little Litany is recited by the Deacon, with the Priest's exclamation: "For Holy art Thou, our God, and unto Thee we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.". Instead of the Trisagion Hymn, the choirs chant the Baptismal Hymn: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia" (Hosoi eis Christon ebaptisthete, Christon enedysasthe. Allelouia, Gal. 3:27). The Epistle of the day is proclaimed: Romans 6:3–11 (Baptized into Christ's Death, Buried with Him through Baptism, That as Christ was Raised from the Dead We Also Should Walk in Newness of Life). At the conclusion of the Epistle, "Alleluia" is omitted. Instead, the Priest emerges from within the Sanctuary and intones in Tone 7 (Grave Tone) the triumphant Verse: "Arise, O God, judge the earth; for Thou shalt inherit among all the nations!" (Anasta ho Theos krinon ten gen, hoti sy katakleronomeseis en pasi tois ethnesi, Ps. 81:8 LXX), while proceeding down the solea and nave, scattering fragrant laurel leaves (bay leaves) throughout the entire temple as an epigraphic symbol of the Lord's victory over death and the shattering of Hades. The choirs repeat this verse after each of the six stichoi of Psalm 81 LXX intoned by the Canonarch: 1. "God standeth in the assembly of gods; in the midst He judgeth gods" (Ps. 81:1 LXX); 2. "How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?" (Ps. 81:2 LXX); 3. "Judge the orphan and the poor; do justice to the humble and needy" (Ps. 81:3 LXX); 4. "Rescue the poor and needy; deliver them out of the hand of the sinner" (Ps. 81:4 LXX); 5. "They have not known, neither have they understood; they walk on in darkness; let all the foundations of the earth be shaken" (Ps. 81:5 LXX); 6. "I said: Ye are gods, and all of you the children of the Most High; but ye die as men, and fall as one of the princes" (Ps. 81:6–7 LXX). After the final stichos, "Arise, O God" is chanted slowly and majestically. The Holy Gospel: Matthew 28:1–20 (The Resurrection of Christ, the appearance of the angel to the women, and the Great Commission: "In the end of the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week..." until "even unto the end of the world") is proclaimed from the ambo. The Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great continues in its regular order. Instead of the customary Cherubic Hymn, the ancient Liturgical Troparion of the Liturgy of Saint James in Tone 5 is chanted: "Let all mortal flesh keep silence, and stand with fear and trembling, and ponder nothing earthly within itself; for the King of kings and Lord of lords cometh forth to be slain, and to be given as food to the faithful. Before Him go the choirs of angels with every principality and power," [during which the solemn Great Entrance is made with the Holy Gifts] "the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim, covering their faces and singing the hymn: Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!" (Sigasato pasa sarx broteia).

[^457]: Great and Holy Saturday: Vespers with the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great Concluded (§ 86 Concluded). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p795 (printed page 780) and facing English leaf p796 (printed page 781). Concluding cadences of the Cherubic Troparion "Let all mortal flesh keep silence": "...covering their faces and crying aloud the hymn: Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia!" [thrice]. The Communion Hymn is chanted: "The Lord awoke as if from sleep, and is risen saving us. Alleluia" (Exegethe hos ho hypnon Kyrios, kai aneste sozon hemas, Allelouia, Ps. 77:65 LXX). Instead of "We have seen the true light" (Eidomen to phos), the choirs chant the Troparion in Tone 2 in a heirmologic melody: "Remember us also, O compassionate One, even as Thou didst remember the thief in the Kingdom of Heaven" (Mnesthiti eusplanchnos kai hemon, kathos emnemoneusas tou Lestou en te Basileia ton Ouranon). The Thanksgiving Hymn: "Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore" (Eie to onoma Kyriou) is sung three times. The solemn Dismissal of the Divine Liturgy is given with the Resurrectional incipit: "May He Who rose from the dead, Christ our true God, through the intercessions of His all-pure and blameless holy Mother, and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind" (Ho anastas ek nekron, Christos ho alethinos Theos hemon...), because the Vespers of Great and Holy Sunday [Pascha] has already been celebrated in anticipation prior to the Liturgy. Violakis notes the foundational canonical reference to General Provisions [Protheoria], Paragraph 16, and the official Report of the Typikon Committee published in the Preface of the 1888 Typikon.

[^458]: Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Holy Pascha (The Midnight Office Opening). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p797 (printed page 782) and facing English leaf p798 (printed page 783). Major structural division: Ritual Order of the Services of the Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Pascha (Mesonyktikon / Midnight Office). At around the Fifth Hour of the night (11:00 p.m.), the clergy and faithful enter into the temple. The Priest intones the opening blessing: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (Eulogetos ho Theos); the Patriarch says: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King, Comforter, the Spirit of truth..." (Basileu ouranie); the Reader recites the Trisagion Prayers, "Lord, have mercy" (12 times), "Glory... Both now and ever...", "Come, let us worship" (thrice), and Psalm 50 LXX plainly. The choirs chant the monumental Holy Saturday Canon in Tone 6: "Of old the surge of the sea covered the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves..." (Kymati thalasses) for six Troparia, each preceded by the refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"; after each Ode, the Heirmos is chanted slowly as Katavasia; the Sessional Hymn [Kathisma] is omitted. At the Fourth Ode, the deacons, vested in their sacred vestments, exit from the Sanctuary bearing the two-branched and three-branched candlesticks [dikirotrikira]. The Patriarch, having venerated the holy icons and prepared himself according to custom for the Divine Liturgy, enters the Sanctuary and vests in all his hierarchical vestments, as do all the concelebrating Hierarchs. Following the Ninth Ode of the Canon, the Trisagion Prayers are recited from within the Sanctuary; then the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 2: "When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brilliance of Thy Divinity..." (Hote katelthes pros ton thanaton); the Augmented Litany and the Dismissal of the Midnight Office are given. The Patriarch, preceded by the concelebrating Hierarchs, exits from the Sanctuary, chanting slowly with them the Sticheron in Tone 6: "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, the angels hymn in the heavens: enable us also on earth to glorify Thee with a pure heart" (Ten Anastasin sou Christe Soter), which is repeated also by the choirs until the procession reaches the appointed outdoor platform [dais / ambo]. Printed Footnote 1 of Violakis: Records the widespread local custom wherein the presiding Hierarch stands before the Beautiful Gate holding the two-branched and three-branched candlestick [dikirotrikiron] lit from the sleepless lamp upon the Holy Table, chanting: "Come, receive the light from the unwaning Light, and glorify Christ Who is risen from the dead!" (Deute labete phos ek tou anesperou photos), and summons the congregation to light their tapers. A translator's scholarly reference cites Alkiviadis C. Calivas's liturgical treatise *Great Week and Pascha in the Greek Orthodox Church* (pages 97–121) regarding the historical evolution of Holy Week and Paschal services.

[^459]: Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Holy Pascha (Paschal Matins: The Resurrection Service and Canon). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p799 (printed page 784) and facing English leaf p800 (printed page 785). Continuation of the Paschal Service at the outdoor platform: The Archdeacon exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel, let us pray unto the Lord God" (Kai hyper tou kataxiothenai hemas). The Patriarch proclaims the Holy Gospel: "In the end of the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week..." (Opse sabbaton te epiphoskouse) [Matthew 28:1–20]. The choirs sing: "Many years to you, Master!" (Eis polla ete, Despota). Printed Footnote 2 of Violakis: Documents the liturgical practice in large cathedrals where this Gospel is proclaimed collaboratively by multiple Hierarchs and Priests, dividing the pericopes at verse 10 and continuing at verse 16 (omitting verses 11–15); it also notes the alternative tradition observed in various monasteries and parishes of proclaiming the Second Eothinon Gospel: "When the Sabbath was past" (Diagenomenou tou Sabbatou, Mark 16:1–8). The Patriarch takes the censer, censes the Holy Gospel Book three times, and intones the solemn Paschal Doxology: "Glory to the holy, and consubstantial, and life-creating, and undivided Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (Doxa te hagia kai homoousio kai zoopoio kai adiaireto Triadi). The Patriarch sings the Paschal Troparion in Tone 5: "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!" (Christos aneste ek nekron) three times; the choirs repeat it six times, while the Patriarch censes and intones the four Paschal Verses of Psalm 67 LXX: 1. "Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered; let them also that hate Him flee before Him!" (Ps. 67:2 LXX); 2. "As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish; as wax melteth before the fire!" (Ps. 67:3 LXX); 3. "So let the wicked perish at the presence of God; and let the righteous be glad!" (Ps. 67:3 LXX); 4. "This is the day which the Lord hath made; let us rejoice and be glad in it!" (Ps. 117:24 LXX), followed by "Glory... Both now and ever...". The Patriarch sings the Troparion once more while censing the clergy and people. The Archdeacon recites the Great Litany: "In peace let us pray unto the Lord" (En eirene tou Kyriou deetnomen), and the Patriarch sings the Exclamation: "For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (Hoti prepei soi pasa doxa). The clergy and people process back into the temple in solemn order. The Patriarch begins chanting the Paschal Canon of Saint John of Damascus in Tone 1: "It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant, O ye peoples!" (Anastaseos hemera) with the concelebrating Hierarchs, with six Troparia in each Ode preceded by the verse: "Glory to Thy holy Resurrection, O Lord!" (Doxa te hagia Anastasei sou, Kyrie); the final two Troparia are preceded by "Glory..." and "Both now and ever...". After each Ode, the Katavasia is chanted, followed by the Little Litany and the appointed Exclamations: Ode 1: "For Thine is the dominion..."; Ode 3: "For Thou art our God..."; Ode 4: "For Thou art a good God, and lovest mankind..."; Ode 5: "For sanctified and glorified is Thine all-honorable and majestic Name..."; Ode 6: "For Thou art the King of peace, and the Savior of our souls..."; Ode 7: "Blessed and glorified be the might of Thy kingdom..."; Ode 8: "For blessed is Thy Name, and glorified is Thy kingdom..."; Ode 9: "For all the powers of the heavens praise Thee...". After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoe: "Anticipating the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..." (Prolabousai ton orthron) is read plainly. After the 6th Ode, the Paschal Kontakion, Ikos, and Synaxarion Memorial of the day are recited; then the Resurrectional hymn: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the Holy Lord Jesus, the only sinless One..." (Anastasin Christou theasamenoi) is chanted three times (once by the Patriarch and twice by the concelebrating Hierarchs), followed by "Jesus having risen from the tomb, as He foretold, hath given us eternal life and great mercy" (Anastas ho Iesous apo tou taphou). Odes 7 and 8 follow; the Great Archdeacon exclaims: "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!", and the 9th Ode is chanted with the appointed Paschal Megalynaria.

[^460]: Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Holy Pascha (Paschal Matins Concluded: Ode 9 Megalynaria, Praises, and Liturgy Opening). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p801 (printed page 786) and facing English leaf p802 (printed page 787). Concluding rubrics of Paschal Matins: At the Ninth Ode of the Paschal Canon of Saint John of Damascus in Tone 1, the appointed Megalynaria are chanted with their Troparia: 1. "Magnify, O my soul, Him Who suffered willingly, and was buried, and arose from the grave on the third day!" (Megalynon psyche mou ton ethelousios pathonta) with the Heirmos: "Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and do thou, O pure Theotokos, rejoice in the Resurrection of Him Whom thou didst bear!" (Photizou, photizou he nea Ierousalem); 2. "Magnify, O my soul, Christ the Giver of life, Who arose from the grave on the third day!" (Megalynon psyche mou ton exanastanta trihemeron ek taphou Christon ton zoodoten) with the same Heirmos repeated; 3. "Christ is the new Pascha, the living sacrificial Victim, the Lamb of God Who taketh away the sin of the world!" (Christos to kainon Pascha) with the Troparion: "O Thy divine, O Thy beloved, O Thy sweetest voice!..." (O theias, o philes); 4. "Today the whole creation is glad and does rejoice, for Christ has risen, and Hades has been despoiled!" (Semeron pasa ktisis agalletai kai chairei) with the same Troparion repeated; "Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit": "Magnify, O my soul, the dominion of the Undivided Godhead of Three Hypostases!" (Megalynon psyche mou, tes Trisypostatou kai adiairetou Theotetos to kratos) with the Troparion: "O great and most sacred Pascha, Christ! O Wisdom, and Word of God, and Power!..." (O Pascha to Mega kai hierotaton, Christe); "Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen": "Rejoice, O Virgin, rejoice; rejoice, O blessed one; rejoice, O most glorified one, for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day!" (Chaire Parthene, chaire, chaire, eulogemene) with the same Troparion repeated. The Katavasia is chanted: "The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..." (Ho Angelos eboa te Kecharitomene). The Little Litany [Petition] is recited, and the Exaposteilarion in Tone 2: "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst rise again, raising up Adam from corruption and abolishing death: O Pascha of incorruption, salvation of the world!" (Sarki hypnosas hos thnetos) is sung three times. At the Praises, eight stichoi are set, chanting the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1 ("We hymn Thy saving Passion, O Christ...", "Thou Who didst endure the Cross...", "Thou Who didst despoil Hades...", "Glorifying Thy divine condescension...") and the four Stichera of Pascha in Tone 5 with their verses of Psalm 67 LXX ("Let God arise...", "A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today...", "As smoke vanisheth...", "Come from that vision, O women...", "So let the wicked perish...", "The myrrh-bearing women...", "This is the day which the Lord hath made...", "A Pascha of delight! Pascha, the Lord's Pascha!..."). "Glory... Both now and ever...": Paschal Doxastikon in Tone 5: "It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another. Let us say, Brethren, even to those who hate us; let us forgive all things at the Resurrection, and thus let us cry:". At the words "and thus let us cry", the Second Choir sings the customary melody of "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!" (Christos aneste); then the First Choir chants the same, and again the Second Choir repeats it, and the Divine Liturgy begins. Printed Footnote 3 of Violakis: Documents that while this Doxastikon is chanted, the solemn veneration of the Holy Gospel Book takes place in all reverence and due order; in certain local traditions, however, the veneration is performed immediately at the beginning of the Paschal Canon for greater convenience of both the clergy and the congregation.

[^461]: Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Holy Pascha (The Divine Liturgy Opening) (§ 2 Opening). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p803 (printed page 788) and facing English leaf p804 (printed page 789). Paragraph 2: The Divine Liturgy of Holy Pascha: The Archdeacon exclaims: "Bless, Master!" (Eulogeson Despota); the Priest intones the Kingdom Doxology: "Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (Eulogemene he basileia), and the choirs respond: "Amen". Directly from within the Sanctuary, the celebrant chants the Paschal Troparion in Tone 5: "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!" (Christos aneste ek nekron) three times; the choirs then sing it six times with the Paschal Verses of Psalm 67 LXX ("Let God arise...", "As smoke vanisheth...", "So let the wicked perish...", "This is the day which the Lord hath made..."), and the final repetition is intoned again from within the Sanctuary. The Festal Antiphons of Pascha are chanted antiphonally with their appointed refrains: Antiphon 1: Psalm 65 LXX ("Shout joyfully unto the Lord, all the earth; chant now unto His Name, give glory unto His praise", "Say unto God: How awesome are Thy works! In the multitude of Thy power shall Thine enemies lie unto Thee", "Let all the earth worship Thee, and chant unto Thee; let them chant unto Thy Name, O Most High!") with the refrain: "Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us!" (Tais presbeiais tes Theotokou, Soter, soson hemas); Antiphon 2: Psalm 66 LXX ("May God be compassionate unto us, and bless us; may He cause His face to shine upon us, and have mercy on us", "That we may know Thy way upon the earth, Thy salvation among all nations", "Let the peoples give thanks unto Thee, O God; let all the peoples give thanks unto Thee!") with the refrain: "Save us, O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead, who sing to Thee: Alleluia!" (Soson hemas Yie Theou, ho anastas ek nekron, psallontas soi, Allelouia); Antiphon 3: Psalm 67 LXX ("Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered...", "As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish...", "So let the wicked perish at the presence of God; and let the righteous be glad!", "This is the day which the Lord hath made; let us rejoice and be glad in it!") with the refrain: "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!". At the Little Entrance, the clergy chant the Entrance Hymn [Isodikon]: "In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel!" (En ekklesiais eulogeite ton Theon, Kyrion ek pegon Israel, Ps. 67:27 LXX).

[^462]: Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Holy Pascha (The Divine Liturgy Concluded) (§ 2 Concluded) and Paschal Vespers Opening (§ 3 Opening). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p805 (printed page 790) and facing English leaf p806 (printed page 791). Concluding rubrics of Paragraph 2 (The Divine Liturgy of Pascha): The Entrance Hymn is completed with the Paschal refrain: "Save us, O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead, who sing to Thee: Alleluia!". Directly after the Entrance: the Troparion "Christ is risen from the dead...", the Ypakoe in Tone 4: "Anticipating the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..." (Prolabousai ton orthron), and the Kontakion in Tone 8: "Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One, yet didst Thou destroy the power of Hades..." (Ei kai en tapho katelthes). In place of the Trisagion Hymn, the Baptismal Hymn: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia" (Hosoi eis Christon ebaptisthete, Gal. 3:27) is chanted. The Epistle is proclaimed: Acts 1:1–8 (The Acts of the Apostles: The Promise of the Father and the Ascension); the "Alleluia" with its verses; and the Holy Gospel: John 1:1–17 (The Paschal Prologue: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God..."). In place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk], the choirs chant the Ninth Heirmos with its Megalynarion: "The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Dance now and be glad, O Zion, and do thou, O pure Theotokos, rejoice in the Resurrection of Him Whom thou didst bear!" (Ho Angelos eboa... Photizou, photizou). The Communion Hymn is chanted: "Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!" (Soma Christou metalabete, peges athanatou geusasthe. Allelouia). After the Prayer behind the Ambo, the Troparion "Christ is risen from the dead..." is intoned three times plainly, and the Patriarch reads from the ambo the monumental Catechetical Sermon of Saint John Chrysostom: "If any be pious and a lover of God, let him enjoy this fair and radiant triumph! If any be a wise servant, let him rejoicing enter into the joy of his Lord!..." (Ei tis eusebes kai philotheos). At its conclusion, the Dismissal Troparion of Saint John Chrysostom in Tone 8 is chanted: "Grace shining forth from thy mouth like a radiant torch has enlightened the universe; it has disclosed to the world the treasures of poverty, and demonstrated to us the height of humility; but as thou dost instruct us by thy words, Father John Chrysostom, intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved!" (He tou stomatos sou kathaper pyrsos eklampsasa charis); the blessing of the Lord is given, and the solemn Dismissal is pronounced by the Patriarch, who exclaims three times: "Christ is risen!", the people responding thrice: "Truly He is risen!". The Patriarch exclaims: "Glory to His holy third-day Resurrection!", the people responding: "We worship His third-day Resurrection!", and the Patriarch concludes by singing the entire Troparion "Christ is risen from the dead...". Following the Dismissal, the Patriarch and concelebrating Hierarchs in full vestments, preceded by taper-bearers, processional fans [hexapteryga], and church officers, ascend to the Great Synodikon while the choirs chant "Christ is risen from the dead...", where the Polychronismos of the Patriarch is chanted according to custom. Paragraph 3 Opening: The Vespers of Pascha [Agape Vespers]: Around the Third Hour of the day [9:00 a.m.], the Patriarch and Hierarchs assemble in the Great Synodikon and vest in their hierarchical vestments, attended by priests and deacons already vested. Printed Footnotes 4–8 of Violakis: Footnote 4: The Entrance Hymn "In the congregations" is chanted daily at the Divine Liturgy until the Apodosis of Pascha; Footnote 5: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ" replaces the Trisagion until Saturday of Bright Week and on the Apodosis; Footnote 6: Chanting "Christ is risen" three times after the Prayer behind the Ambo continues until Saturday of Bright Week, whereas from Thomas Sunday onward "Blessed be the name of the Lord" is sung; Footnote 7: In ancient Typika, Chrysostom's Catechetical Sermon was read after the Praises before the Divine Liturgy as preparation for Holy Communion, but later practice permanently fixed it after the Communion Hymn or Prayer behind the Ambo; Footnote 8: From Holy Pascha until Saturday of Bright Week, and on the Apodosis, the entire liturgical cycle of the Hours (First, Third, Sixth, Ninth Hours), Compline, and Midnight Office is replaced by the Paschal Service: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", "Christ is risen from the dead" (thrice), "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" (thrice), the Ypakoe "Anticipating the dawn...", the Kontakion "Though Thou didst descend into the grave...", the Troparia "In the tomb bodily...", "Glory...", "As life-bearing...", "Both now and ever...", "That which is sanctified by the Most High...", "Lord, have mercy" (40 times), "Glory... Both now and ever...", "More honorable than the Cherubim", "Through the prayers of our holy fathers...", and "Christ is risen from the dead" (thrice). This service is repeated three times daily in place of the regular offices.

[^463]: Pentekostarion: The Sunday of Holy Pascha (Paschal Agape Vespers Concluded) (§ 3 Concluded). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p807 (printed page 792) and facing English leaf p808 (printed page 793). Concluding rubrics of Paragraph 3 (The Vespers of Love / Agape Vespers): While the Patriarch and concelebrating Hierarchs vest in the Great Synodikon, the choirs chant the slow Paschal Heirmos in Tone 1: "It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant, O ye peoples!" (Anastaseos hemera argon). A solemn procession forms: led by candle-bearers, processional fans [hexapteryga], the Primikirios, and the choirs chanting "Christ is risen from the dead...", followed by priests, Hierarchs, deacons holding the two-branched and three-branched candlesticks [dikirotrikira], and finally the Patriarch bearing his pastoral staff and the Holy Gospel Book, escorted by the Grand Logothete, ambassadors of Orthodox nations, and civil dignitaries. Processing down into the church, the Patriarch and clergy enter directly into the Sanctuary. The Patriarch censes three times before the Holy Table and intones the opening doxology: "Glory to the holy, and consubstantial, and life-creating, and undivided Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", singing "Christ is risen from the dead..." according to the order of Paschal Matins. The Great Litany is recited by the Archdeacon, and the Patriarch intones the exclamation: "For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship...". At "Lord, I have cried" (Kyrie ekekraxa), six Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2 are chanted in order: "Before the ages, begotten of the Father, God the Word incarnate of the Virgin Mary, come, let us worship; for having endured the Cross, He was delivered over to burial, as He Himself willed, and having risen from the dead, He saved me, the wandering man!" (Ton pro aionon ek Patros gennethenta), while the Patriarch, preceded by the Primikirios bearing the two-branched candle [divamvoulon], censes the icons and congregation, and ascends the throne. The First Choir sings "Glory...": "The saving hymn we sing with our mouths: Come, let us all worship in the house of the Lord..." (Ton soterion hymnon); the Second Choir sings "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 2: "The shadow of the law passed away when grace arrived..." (Parelthen he skia tou nomou). The Little Entrance is made with the Holy Gospel Book; "O Gladsome Light" (Phos hilaron) is chanted slowly and entirely outside the Sanctuary. The Patriarch enters the Sanctuary singing the Great Prokimenon in Tone 7: "What God is as great as our God? Thou art the God Who workest wonders!" (Tis Theos megas hos ho Theos hemon; sy ei ho Theos ho poion thaumasia, Ps. 76:14 LXX) with its three verses (Ps. 76:15, 11, 12 LXX), repeated antiphonally by the choirs. The Patriarch exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy to hear the Holy Gospel, let us pray unto the Lord God", and proclaims the Holy Gospel: John 20:19–25 ("When it was evening on that day, the first day of the week..." until "Except I shall see in His hands the print of the nails... I will not believe"), proclaimed in successive pericopes and translated/echoed in multiple languages by the concelebrating Hierarchs, priests, and deacons. After the choirs chant "Many years to you, Master!" (Eis polla ete), the Augmented Litany, "Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin", and the Evening Litany are recited. After the exclamation: "Blessed and glorified be the might of Thy kingdom: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", the First Choir chants the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 2: "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, hath enlightened the whole universe and recalled Thine own creation: O almighty Lord, glory to Thee!" (He Anastasis sou Christe Soter), followed by the Stichera of Pascha: "A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..." (Pascha hieron), "Glory... Both now and ever...": "It is the day of Resurrection...", and "Christ is risen from the dead..." (three times). During this chanting, the Patriarch and clergy process back up to the Great Synodikon, where the Patriarch gives the solemn Dismissal while the choirs chant his Polychronismos; thus concluding the Agape Vespers.

[^464]: Bright Week: Bright Monday (§§ 4–5) and Bright Friday: The Life-Giving Fountain Opening (§ 6 Opening). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p809 (printed page 794) and facing English leaf p810 (printed page 795). Paragraph 4: Monday of Bright Week Matins: Following the Paschal replacement service for the Midnight Office (Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest, fully vested in all priestly vestments, stands before the Holy Table with the censer, censes, and intones: "Glory to the holy, and consubstantial, and life-creating, and undivided Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen."; he then chants "Christ is risen from the dead..." three times with the Paschal Verses. The Litany is recited with the exclamation: "For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship...". The Paschal Canon of Saint John of Damascus in Tone 1 is chanted without variation, except that after Ode 6 only the Kontakion ("Though Thou didst descend into the grave...") is said, followed directly by "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." (once). After Ode 8, the Deacon intones: "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!", and Ode 9 is sung with the Megalynaria. The Exaposteilarion: "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal..." is sung twice according to ancient typika. At the Praises, four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2 ("Let every breath and all creation glorify Thee, O Lord...") and the Stichera of Pascha ("A sacred Pascha...") are chanted with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": "It is the day of Resurrection...", "Christ is risen from the dead..." (three times), and the Divine Liturgy begins. Paragraph 5: Monday of Bright Week Divine Liturgy: The Antiphons are celebrated as on Pascha Sunday. In place of the Trisagion, "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia" (Gal. 3:27) is sung; the Epistle (Acts 1:12–17, 21–26) and Holy Gospel (Luke 24:12–35: The Road to Emmaus) of the day are proclaimed. In place of "It is truly right", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: "The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace... Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..." is chanted. Communion Hymn: "Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!". After the Prayer behind the Ambo, "Christ is risen from the dead..." is intoned three times plainly, followed by the Dismissal. General Rubric for Bright Week: This identical order of service is to be strictly observed on each day throughout the entirety of Bright Week at Vespers, Matins, and the Divine Liturgy, with the sole exception of the Gospel reading proclaimed at the Vespers of Pascha Sunday afternoon. Paragraph 6: Friday of Bright Week: The Feast of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos of the Life-Giving Fountain: On Thursday evening at "Lord, I have cried" (Kyrie ekekraxa), ten Stichera are chanted: six Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3: "Holding the victory, O Christ, over Hades, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, that Thou mightest raise up with Thyself those who sat in the darkness of death: O Free among the dead, Who pourest forth life from Thine own light, almighty Savior, have mercy on us!" (Niken echon Christe) and four of the Life-Giving Fountain in Tone 3, repeating the first: 1. & 2. "Who can declare thy mighty wonders, O Fountain? For flowing with streams of wonders, thou dost pour forth rivers of healings..." (Tis lalesei tas dynasteias sou Pege). "Glory...": Doxastikon of the Fountain in Tone 6: "Who can tell of thy mighty acts, O undefiled Fountain? For abundant in miracles and lavish in grace, thou dost ever pour forth healings..." (Tis lalesei tas dynasteias sou Pege); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 3: "Who would not admire, who would not praise thy childbirth without seed, O all-pure Virgin? For the Son Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, the Only-Begotten One, came forth from thee, pure Maiden, ineffably incarnate: God by nature, yet for our sakes becoming man by nature..." (Tis me makarisei se, Panagia Parthene). The Little Entrance is made with the censer; "O Gladsome Light" (Phos hilaron) is chanted, followed by the Great Prokimenon in Tone 7: "I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my foundation, my refuge, and my deliverer!" (Agapeso se, Kyrie, he ischys mou, Ps. 17:2–3 LXX) with its appointed verses. At the Aposticha, begun by the Second Choir, the Resurrectional Sticheron: "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior..." (Ten Anastasin sou Christe Soter) is chanted.

Concluding rubrics of Paschal Matins: At the Ninth Ode of the Paschal Canon of Saint John of Damascus in Tone 1, the appointed Megalynaria are chanted with their Troparia: 1. "Magnify, O my soul, Him Who suffered willingly, and was buried, and arose from the grave on the third day!" (Megalynon psyche mou ton ethelousios pathonta) with the Heirmos: "Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem, for the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee! Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..." (Ho Angelos eboa te Kecharitomene). The Little Litany [Petition] is recited, and the Exaposteilarion in Tone 2: "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst rise again, raising up Adam from corruption and abolishing death: O Pascha of incorruption, salvation of the world!" (Sarki hypnosas hos thnetos) is sung three times. At the Praises, eight stichoi are set, chanting the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1 ("We hymn Thy saving Passion, O Christ...", "Thou Who didst endure the Cross...", "Thou Who didst despoil Hades...", "Glorifying Thy divine condescension...") and the four Stichera of Pascha in Tone 5 with their verses of Psalm 67 LXX ("Let God arise...", "A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today...", "As smoke vanisheth...", "Come from that vision, O women...", "So let the wicked perish...", "The myrrh-bearing women...", "This is the day which the Lord hath made...", "A Pascha of delight! Pascha, the Lord's Pascha!..."). "Glory... Both now and ever...": Paschal Doxastikon in Tone 5: "It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another. Let us say, Brethren, even to those who hate us; let us forgive all things at the Resurrection, and thus let us cry:". At the words "and thus let us cry", the Second Choir sings the customary melody of "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!" (Christos aneste); then the First Choir chants the same, and again the Second Choir repeats it, and the Divine Liturgy begins. Printed Footnote 3 of Violakis: Documents that while this Doxastikon is chanted, the solemn veneration of the Holy Gospel Book takes place in all reverence and due order; in certain local traditions, however, the veneration is performed immediately at the beginning of the Paschal Canon for greater convenience of both the clergy and the congregation.

Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p803 (printed page 788) and facing English leaf p804 (printed page 789). Paragraph 2: The Divine Liturgy of Holy Pascha: The Archdeacon exclaims: "Bless, Master!" (Eulogeson Despota); the Priest intones the Kingdom Doxology: "Blessed is the kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (Eulogemene he basileia), and the choirs respond: "Amen". Directly from within the Sanctuary, the celebrant chants the Paschal Troparion in Tone 5: "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!" (Christos aneste ek nekron) three times; the choirs then sing it six times with the Paschal Verses of Psalm 67 LXX ("Let God arise...", "As smoke vanisheth...", "So let the wicked perish...", "This is the day which the Lord hath made..."), and the final repetition is intoned again from within the Sanctuary. The Festal Antiphons of Pascha are chanted antiphonally with their appointed refrains: Antiphon 1: Psalm 65 LXX ("Shout joyfully unto the Lord, all the earth; chant now unto His Name, give glory unto His praise", "Say unto God: How awesome are Thy works! In the multitude of Thy power shall Thine enemies lie unto Thee", "Let all the earth worship Thee, and chant unto Thee; let them chant unto Thy Name, O Most High!") with the refrain: "Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us!" (Tais presbeiais tes Theotokou, Soter, soson hemas); Antiphon 2: Psalm 66 LXX ("May God be compassionate unto us, and bless us; may He cause His face to shine upon us, and have mercy on us", "That we may know Thy way upon the earth, Thy salvation among all nations", "Let the peoples give thanks unto Thee, O God; let all the peoples give thanks unto Thee!") with the refrain: "Save us, O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead, who sing to Thee: Alleluia!" (Soson hemas Yie Theou, ho anastas ek nekron, psallontas soi, Allelouia); Antiphon 3: Psalm 67 LXX ("Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered...", "As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish...", "So let the wicked perish at the presence of God; and let the righteous be glad!", "This is the day which the Lord hath made; let us rejoice and be glad in it!") with the refrain: "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!". At the Little Entrance, the clergy chant the Entrance Hymn [Isodikon]: "In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel!" (En ekklesiais eulogeite ton Theon, Kyrion ek pegon Israel, Ps. 67:27 LXX).

Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p805 (printed page 790) and facing English leaf p806 (printed page 791). Concluding rubrics of Paragraph 2 (The Divine Liturgy of Pascha): The Entrance Hymn is completed with the Paschal refrain: "Save us, O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead, who sing to Thee: Alleluia!". Directly after the Entrance: the Troparion "Christ is risen from the dead...", the Ypakoe in Tone 4: "Anticipating the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..." (Prolabousai ton orthron), and the Kontakion in Tone 8: "Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One, yet didst Thou destroy the power of Hades..." (Ei kai en tapho katelthes). In place of the Trisagion Hymn, the Baptismal Hymn: "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia" (Hosoi eis Christon ebaptisthete, Gal. 3:27) is chanted. The Epistle is proclaimed: Acts 1:1–8 (The Acts of the Apostles: The Promise of the Father and the Ascension); the "Alleluia" with its verses; and the Holy Gospel: John 1:1–17 (The Paschal Prologue: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God..."). In place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk], the choirs chant the Ninth Heirmos with its Megalynarion: "The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day. (Ho Angelos eboa... Photizou, photizou). The Communion Hymn is chanted: "Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!" (Soma Christou metalabete, peges athanatou geusasthe. Allelouia). After the Prayer behind the Ambo, the Troparion "Christ is risen from the dead..." is intoned three times plainly, and the Patriarch reads from the ambo the monumental Catechetical Sermon of Saint John Chrysostom: "If any be pious and a lover of God, let him enjoy this fair and radiant triumph! If any be a wise servant, let him rejoicing enter into the joy of his Lord!..." (Ei tis eusebes kai philotheos). At its conclusion, the Dismissal Troparion of Saint John Chrysostom in Tone 8 is chanted: "Grace shining forth from thy mouth like a radiant torch has enlightened the universe; it has disclosed to the world the treasures of poverty, and demonstrated to us the height of humility; but as thou dost instruct us by thy words, Father John Chrysostom, intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved!" (He tou stomatos sou kathaper pyrsos eklampsasa charis); the blessing of the Lord is given, and the solemn Dismissal is pronounced by the Patriarch, who exclaims three times: "Christ is risen!", the people responding thrice: "Truly He is risen!". The Patriarch exclaims: "Glory to His holy third-day Resurrection!", the people responding: "We worship His third-day Resurrection!", and the Patriarch concludes by singing the entire Troparion "Christ is risen from the dead...". Following the Dismissal, the Patriarch and concelebrating Hierarchs in full vestments, preceded by taper-bearers, processional fans [hexapteryga], and church officers, ascend to the Great Synodikon while the choirs chant "Christ is risen from the dead...", where the Polychronismos of the Patriarch is chanted according to custom. The Paschal Canon of Saint John of Damascus in Tone 1 is chanted without variation, except that after Ode 6 only the Kontakion ("Though Thou didst descend into the grave...") is said, followed directly by "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." (once). After Ode 8, the Deacon intones: "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in hymns!", and Ode 9 is sung with the Megalynaria. The Exaposteilarion: "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal..." is sung twice according to ancient typika. At the Praises, four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 2 ("Let every breath and all creation glorify Thee, O Lord...") and the Stichera of Pascha ("A sacred Pascha...") are chanted with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": "It is the day of Resurrection...", "Christ is risen from the dead..." (three times), and the Divine Liturgy begins. Paragraph 5: Monday of Bright Week Divine Liturgy: The Antiphons are celebrated as on Pascha Sunday. In place of the Trisagion, "As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia" (Gal. 3:27) is sung; the Epistle (Acts 1:12–17, 21–26) and Holy Gospel (Luke 24:12–35: The Road to Emmaus) of the day are proclaimed. In place of "It is truly right", the Ninth Heirmos with Megalynarion: "The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace... Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..." is chanted. Communion Hymn: "Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!". After the Prayer behind the Ambo, "Christ is risen from the dead..." is intoned three times plainly, followed by the Dismissal. General Rubric for Bright Week: This identical order of service is to be strictly observed on each day throughout the entirety of Bright Week at Vespers, Matins, and the Divine Liturgy, with the sole exception of the Gospel reading proclaimed at the Vespers of Pascha Sunday afternoon. Paragraph 6: Friday of Bright Week: The Feast of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos of the Life-Giving Fountain: On Thursday evening at "Lord, I have cried" (Kyrie ekekraxa), ten Stichera are chanted: six Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 3: "Holding the victory, O Christ, over Hades, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, that Thou mightest raise up with Thyself those who sat in the darkness of death: O Free among the dead, Who pourest forth life from Thine own light, almighty Savior, have mercy on us!" (Niken echon Christe) and four of the Life-Giving Fountain in Tone 3, repeating the first: 1. & 2. "Who can declare thy mighty wonders, O Fountain? For flowing with streams of wonders, thou dost pour forth rivers of healings..." (Tis lalesei tas dynasteias sou Pege). "Glory...": Doxastikon of the Fountain in Tone 6: "Who can tell of thy mighty acts, O undefiled Fountain? For abundant in miracles and lavish in grace, thou dost ever pour forth healings..." (Tis lalesei tas dynasteias sou Pege); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 3: "Who would not admire, who would not praise thy childbirth without seed, O all-pure Virgin? For the Son Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, the Only-Begotten One, came forth from thee, pure Maiden, ineffably incarnate: God by nature, yet for our sakes becoming man by nature..." (Tis me makarisei se, Panagia Parthene). The Little Entrance is made with the censer; "O Gladsome Light" (Phos hilaron) is chanted, followed by the Great Prokimenon in Tone 7: "I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my foundation, my refuge, and my deliverer!" (Agapeso se, Kyrie, he ischys mou, Ps. 17:2–3 LXX) with its appointed verses. At the Aposticha, begun by the Second Choir, the Resurrectional Sticheron: "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior..." (Ten Anastasin sou Christe Soter) is chanted.

(*Κύριε τὸν Παράλυτον*); "Both now and ever...": Tone 5: "It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another!..." (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*); Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion: "Today is salvation come into the world: let us sing unto Him Who arose from the tomb, the Author of our life!..." (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*). Paragraph 22: Sunday of the Paralytic Divine Liturgy: Paschal Antiphons and the Entrance Hymn of Pascha. After the Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 3: "Let the heavens rejoice, let earthly things be glad!..." (*Εὐφραινέσθω τὰ Οὐράνια*), that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion of Pascha: "Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..." (*Εἰ καὶ ἐν τάφῳ*). The Epistle (Acts 9:32–42) and Gospel (John 5:1–15) of the Sunday. At "Especially", in place of "It is truly right" [Axion Estin / Zadostoinyk]: "The Angel cried unto her who is full of grace: O pure Virgin, rejoice, and again I say rejoice; for thy Son has arisen from the grave on the third day..." (*Ὁ Ἄγγελος ἐβόα*), with the Ninth Heirmos of the Canon: "With one voice, O Virgin, we bless thee: Hail, gate of the Lord, through which none may pass!..." (*Συμφώνως Παρθένε*) [Printed Note 12 of Violakis: Documents that it has become the customary practice on this Sunday and the following, perhaps for variety, to chant the Theotokia of the Canon instead of "Shine, shine, O new Jerusalem..."]. Communion Hymn: "Receive the Body of Christ; taste of the immortal Fountain. Alleluia!" (*Σῶμα Χριστοῦ*), "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!" (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*), "Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages" (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal. The Service of the Paralytic is chanted until Tuesday, on which day its Apodosis is celebrated. Paragraph 23: The Wednesday of Mid-Pentecost Vespers: On Tuesday evening, after "Christ is risen from the dead...", we recite the Introductory Psalm (Ps. 103 LXX). At "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the three Prosomia: "Now has come the midpoint of the days..." (*Πάρεστιν ἡ μεσότης ἡμερῶν*) to six (twice each); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 6: "As the Feast comes to its midpoint, O Christ God..." (*Τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης*); Entrance with censer, the Prokimenon of the day, and the Old Testament Readings (Micah 4:2–3, 5; 5:2–5, 8; Isaiah 55:1–3, 6–11; Proverbs 9:1–11 LXX). At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela: "The midpoint of the days of Pentecost has arrived..." (*Πεντηκοστῆς ἐφέστηκεν*), with the appointed Verses: "Remember Thy congregation, which Thou hast purchased from the beginning" (*Μνήσθητι τῆς συναγωγῆς σου ἧς ἐκτήσω ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς*, Ps. 73:2 LXX), and "God is our King before the ages: He hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth" (*Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς Βασιλεὺς ἡμῶν πρὸ αἰώνων εἰργάσατο σωτηρίαν ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς*, Ps. 73:12 LXX); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 8: "At the midpoint of the Feast..." (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*); Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8: "At the midpoint of the Feast, provide Thou my thirsty soul with the water of piety, as Thou didst cry unto all, O Savior: Whosoever thirsteth, let him come unto Me and drink! O Well-spring of our life, Christ God, glory to Thee!" (*Μεσούσης τῆς ἑορτῆς*) three times, and Dismissal. Paragraph 24: Wednesday Matins: After the Midnight Office, the Trisagion, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord" (*Θεὸς Κύριος*): the Dismissal Troparion in Tone 8 (three times); then the Psalter; then the two Kathismata of the First and Second Stasis of the Kathisma [Stichologia], twice each; then "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) and Psalm 50 recited plainly. Both Canons without verses. After the 3rd Ode, the two Kathismata; after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion in Tone 4: "As the Feast of the Law is at midpoint, O Creator and Master of all, Thou didst say unto those present, O Christ God: Come and draw forth the water of immortality!..." (*Τῆς ἑορτῆς τῆς νομικῆς μεσαζούσης*), the Ikos, the Menologion of the day, and the Hypomnema of the Feast. The Katavasias: "Thou didst make the sea a wall..." (*Θάλασσαν ἔπηξας*); then the 9th Ode of both Canons, and the Katavasia: "Virginity is alien to mothers, and childbearing is strange to virgins; yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished!..." (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν Μητέρων*); the Exaposteilarion: "Having arrived at the midpoint of the feasts..." (*Ὁ τὸν κρατῆρα ἔχων*) twice. At the Praises: three Prosomia to four (repeating the first); "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 4: "Having been enlightened, brethren, by the Resurrection of Christ the Savior..." (*Φωτισθέντες ἀδελφοί*); Great Doxology and the Dismissal Troparion.

[^474]: Wednesday of the 6th Week: The Apodosis of the Feast of Pascha (§§ 35–36). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p829 (printed page 814) and facing English leaf p830 (printed page 815). Paragraph 35: Tuesday evening: The Ninth Hour is read as tri-psalmic (involving Psalms 83, 84, 85 LXX), at which we say the Dismissal Troparion: "The Word co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit..." (*Τὸν συνάναρχον λόγον*), and the Kontakion: "My soul's eyes being blind, I come unto Thee, O Christ..." (*Τῆς ψυχῆς τὰ ὄμματα*); then, instead of the usual "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", the Priest exclaims (as is the custom now): "Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and indivisible Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (*Δόξα τῇ ἁγίᾳ καὶ ὁμοουσίῳ*). Then the Priest inside the Sanctuary chants "Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life!" (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) three times; this hymn is chanted also three times by each of the two Choirs, and again immediately once by the Priest from the Sanctuary [Note: The rubrics of the Pentekostarion state simply: "And we chant Christ is risen with its verses, exactly as was done on the day of Pascha." Apparently, this exact order is what is actually being called for here: if each of the two Choirs chants "Christ is risen" three times, we have the sum total of 10 times, as on the day of Pascha]. Then the Litany follows. At "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), we chant the six Stichera of the Octoechos in Tone 5: "Accept our evening prayers, O holy Lord, and grant unto us remission of sins; for Thou alone art He Who didst manifest the Resurrection unto the world!" (*Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχὰς*) in order; "Glory...": Doxastikon in Tone 5: "Him Who is co-eternal with the Father and the Spirit, let us praise..." (*Τὸν τῷ Πατρὶ συνάναρχον*); "Both now and ever...": Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 1: "The Joy of all the world, who sprang forth from mankind and gave birth unto the Master..." (*Τὴν παγκόσμιον δόξαν*). Entrance with censer, and the Prokimenon of the day: "Thy mercy, O Lord, shall pursue me all the days of my life!" (*Τὸ ἔλεός σου, Κύριε*, Ps. 22:6 LXX). At the Aposticha: the Resurrectional Apostichon Sticheron in Tone 5: "By Thy Passion, O Christ, hast Thou darkened the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection hast Thou enlightened all things..." (*Τῷ πάθει σου Χριστέ*), then the Stichera of Pascha: "A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..." (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 5: "It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival, and let us embrace one another!..." (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), then "Christ is risen from the dead..." (three times), and Dismissal. Paragraph 36: Wednesday morning Matins of the Apodosis of Pascha: After the Midnight Office of Pascha (see Paragraph 2, Note 8), the Priest censing in front of the Holy Table exclaims: "Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and indivisible Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", and chants "Christ is risen from the dead..." (*Χριστὸς ἀνέστη*) as yesterday; then the Litany, and the Paschal Canon is chanted with four Troparia for each ode including the Katavasia. Then we chant "Christ is risen from the dead..." (three times), the hymn: "Jesus, having arisen from the tomb, as He foretold, hath given unto us life eternal and great mercy!" (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τοῦ τάφου*), the Litany, and the Exclamation at the end of each Ode. After the 3rd Ode, the Ypakoe: "Coming before the dawn, Mary and the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb..." (*Προλαβοῦσαι τὸν Ὄρθρον*) (recited plainly); after the 6th Ode, the Kontakion: "Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One..." and the Ikos of Pascha, then "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the holy Lord Jesus..." (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*) (three times), and "Jesus, having arisen from the tomb..." (*Ἀναστὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς*); then the 7th and 8th Odes of the Canon are chanted. Then the deacon or priest proclaims: "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light, honoring her in hymns, let us magnify!" (*Τὴν Θεοτόκον καὶ Μητέρα τοῦ Φωτός*), and the 9th Ode is chanted with the Megalynaria of Pascha. The Exaposteilarion: "Having slept in the flesh as a mortal, O King and Lord, on the third day Thou didst arise..." (*Σαρκὶ ὑπνώσας ὡς θνητός*) (three times). At the Praises: the four Resurrectional Stichera in Tone 1: "We praise Thy saving Passion, O Christ, and glorify Thy Resurrection!" (*Ὑμνοῦμέν σου Χριστέ*) and the Stichera of Pascha: "A sacred Pascha is shown forth unto us today..." (*Πάσχα ἱερόν*) with their verses; "Glory... Both now and ever...": Tone 5: "It is the day of Resurrection: let us be radiant for the festival..." (*Ἀναστάσεως ἡμέρα*), then "Christ is risen from the dead..." (three times), and the Divine Liturgy begins.

Then the Deacon intones: "Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord...", and the Exclamation: "For Thou art a good God and lovest mankind...". The Patriarch: "Peace be to all"... The Deacon: "Let us bow our heads unto the Lord"; the Patriarch reads the Prayer of Head-inclination and intones the Exclamation: "May the might of Thy Kingdom be blessed and glorified...".

Concluding rubrics of the Divine Liturgy of the Sunday of All Saints: After the Little Entrance, the Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, that of the Saints in Tone 4 ("Clothed in the blood of Thy Martyrs throughout all the world as in purple and fine linen, Thy Church through them crieth unto Thee, O Christ God: Send down Thy compassions upon Thy people; grant peace unto Thy commonwealth, and unto our souls great mercy!"), that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion in Tone 8: "Unto Thee, O Lord, the Planter of creation, the world offereth the God-bearing Martyrs as first-fruits of nature; by their supplications preserve Thy Church and Thy commonwealth in profound peace, through the Theotokos, O Thou Who art greatly merciful!" (*Ὡς ἀπαρχὰς τῆς φύσεως*). The Epistle of the Saints (Hebrews 11:33–12:2) and Gospel of the Saints (Matthew 10:32–33, 37–38; 19:27–30). At "Especially", "It is truly right to bless thee, O Theotokos..." (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: "Rejoice in the Lord, O you righteous, praise is meet for the upright. Alleluia!" (*Ἀγαλλιᾶσθε δίκαιοι ἐν Κυρίῳ, τοῖς εὐθέσι πρέπει αἴνεσις*, Ps. 32:1 LXX); "We have seen the true Light..." (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), "Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth, and unto the ages" (*Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*), and Dismissal. This marks the conclusion of Part II of the Typikon (The Triodion and Pentekostarion Cycles).

[^486]: Typikon Appendix (Supplement): Title Page. Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p853 (printed page 838) and facing English leaf p854 (printed page 839). Half-title leaf introducing the Appendix to the 1888 Violakis Typikon: Greek: ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ ΤΟΥ ΤΥΠΙΚΟΥ; English: TYPIKON APPENDIX. The Appendix contains special ceremonial orders of the Great Church of Christ (Patriarchate of Constantinople), beginning with the solemn Hierarchical Service of the Akathist Hymn on Friday of the Fifth Week of Great Lent.

[^487]: Order of Service of the Akathist Hymn in the Patriarchal Church: Opening Rubrics (§ Appendix 1). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p855 (printed page 840) and facing English leaf p856 (printed page 841). Ceremony of the Akathist Hymn on the Friday evening of the Fifth Week of the Great Fast: At the Ninth Hour [3:00 p.m.], the Ecumenical Patriarch descends with the customary patriarchal entourage into the Narthex, where he vests with the Mandyas [Hierarchical Mantle] and receives the Pastoral Staff (*Pateritsa*). He enters the Nave, blesses the congregation, and ascends the Patriarchal Throne. While the Choirs sing "For many years, Master!" (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, Δέσποτα*), the Great Archimandrite, the Great Archdeacon, and the Second Deacon receive Keron (*καιρόν*)—the formal liturgical blessing and permission to officiate from the Patriarch. The Great Archimandrite intones the opening Exclamation: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Patriarch begins: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!", "O Heavenly King, Comforter, Spirit of truth...". The designated Reader-Priest, standing opposite the Patriarch near the Primikirios, reads the Trisagion Prayers and Small Compline. Following "It is truly right" (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), the First Choir chants the Troparion in Tone 8: "Taking knowledge of the secret command" (*Τὸ προσταχθὲν μυστικῶς*) slowly and melodiously. During this hymn, the officiating Hierarchs exit the Bema through the South Deacon's Gate, led by the Great Ecclesiarch, and take their places in the Soleas according to seniority. [Printed Note 1: Receiving Keron (*καιρόν*) is the formal blessing of the highest-ranking hierarch authorizing clergy to participate in the sacred office. Printed Note 2: Patriarchal court offices (*offikia*) such as Primikirios and Megas Logothetis originated in Byzantine administrative governance and became honorary ceremonial titles in the post-Byzantine Great Church of Christ].

[^488]: Order of Service of the Akathist Hymn in the Patriarchal Church: First Stasis and Opening Odes (§ Appendix 2). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p857 (printed page 842) and facing English leaf p858 (printed page 843). The Great Ecclesiarch, having made a reverent bow (*σχῆμα*) to the Patriarch, returns to the Bema with the Great Archdeacon and Second Deacon. As the Second Choir repeats "Taking knowledge of the secret command" (*Τὸ προσταχθὲν μυστικῶς*), the vested Deacons with Dikerotrikera, led by the Ecclesiarch, exit the Beautiful Gate and flank the Patriarchal Throne. Midway through the hymn, the Patriarch descends, enters the Sanctuary preceded by the Primikirios, Ecclesiarch, and Deacons, kisses the Holy Table, and is vested with Epitrachilion and Omophorion. The Primikirios stands before the Festal Icon of the Theotokos on the Soleas. As the First Choir chants "Taking knowledge..." for the third time at a moderate tempo, the Patriarch exits the Sanctuary, censes the Holy Icon three times, and solemnly intones the First Stasis of the Oikoi (Oikoi 1–6: A–Z / Ἀ–Ζ), censing three times at the end of each Ikos. He then kisses the Icon, blesses the people with the Trikirion while the Choirs sing "For many years, Master!", and returns to the Sanctuary to unvest from the Epitrachilion and Omophorion before re-ascending his Throne. The Choirs sing Odes 1 and 3 of the Canon ("I shall open my mouth and it shall be filled with the Spirit" / *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*), followed by the slow, solemn singing of the Kontakion in Tone 8: "To the Champion General" (*Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ*) by both Choirs. During its penultimate verse, the Great Ecclesiarch invites the first officiating Hierarch to enter the Bema. [Printed Note 3: The reverent sign (*σχῆμα*) consists of placing the right hand over the chest and bowing slightly. Printed Note 4: The Dikerion symbolizes the two natures of Christ (divine and human), and the Trikirion symbolizes the three Persons of the Holy Trinity].

[^489]: Order of Service of the Akathist Hymn in the Patriarchal Church: Stases 2–4, Canon Odes 4–9, and Divamvulon (§ Appendix 3). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p859 (printed page 844) and facing English leaf p860 (printed page 845). The first officiating Hierarch kisses the Patriarch's hand, enters the Sanctuary preceded by the Ecclesiarch, and vests with Epitrachilion and Omophorion. Preceded by the Third Deacon and another Deacon with Dikerotrikera, he exits to the Festal Icon, censes the Patriarch and the Icon three times each, and intones the Second Stasis of the Oikoi (Oikoi 7–12: H–M / Η–Μ). Upon conclusion, he kisses the Icon, bows to the Patriarch, returns to the Bema, unvests, and remains inside. The Choirs sing Odes 4, 5, and 6 of the Canon. During Ode 6, the Ecclesiarch invites the second Hierarch, who receives Keron from the Patriarch, vests in the Bema, and towards the end of the fast "To the Champion General" (*Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ*), exits with the Deacons to intone the Third Stasis of the Oikoi (Oikoi 13–18: N–P / Ν–Π). He unvests in the Bema. The Choirs sing Odes 7, 8, and 9 of the Canon; during Ode 7, the two vested Deacons cense the congregation. During Ode 9, the third Hierarch receives Keron, vests, exits towards the conclusion of "To the Champion General", and intones the Fourth Stasis of the Oikoi (Oikoi 19–24: T–Omega / Τ–Ω, concluding with the repetition of Ikos 1). The remaining Hierarchs in attendance come before the Patriarch in order of seniority, bow, kiss the Festal Icon, and enter the Bema. Following the final rapid singing of "To the Champion General", the Reader recites the Trisagion and Kontakion, and the Primikirios comes forward with the Divamvulon (a large double-branched candlestick) and stands opposite the Patriarchal Throne.

[^490]: Service of the Akathist Hymn Concluded (§ Appendix 4). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p861 (printed page 846) and facing English leaf p862 (printed page 847). Concluding rubrics of the solemn Patriarchal Service of the Akathist Hymn: Following the Fourth Stasis and the entrance with the Divamvulon, the Great Ecclesiarch, Priests, and Deacons take their stations across from and beside the Patriarchal Throne. The Reader-Priest recites "To the Champion General" (*Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ*), the Forty Lord Have Mercies, and the Prayer of the Canonical Hours: "Thou Who at all times and at every hour..." (*Ὁ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ*). The Patriarch recites "May God be merciful unto us and bless us..." (*Ὁ Θεὸς οἰκτιρήσαι ἡμᾶς*), and the Canonarchs chant the Compline prayers: "O Spotless, Undefiled, Incorrupt..." (*Ἄσπιλε, ἀμόλυντε*) and "And grant unto us, O Master..." (*Καὶ δὸς ἡμῖν, Δέσποτα*). The Priest intones the Small Dismissal and the Fervent Supplication for the peace of the world (*Εὐξώμεθα ὑπὲρ εἰρήνης τοῦ κόσμου*). The Choirs sing the slow Kathisma in Tone 3: "Seeing the beauty of thy virginity..." (*Τὴν ὡραιότητα τῆς παρθενίας σου*), during which the Patriarch descends from the Throne, blesses the congregation, and departs, while the Priest concludes with the solemn Patriarchal Dismissal: "Through the prayers of our holy Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen." (*Δι' εὐχῶν τοῦ ἁγίου Δεσπότου ἡμῶν...*). [Printed Note: At the Dismissal, when the Patriarch himself concludes or prior to the priest's exclamation, the Patriarch proclaims: "Through the prayers of our Holy Fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen."].

[^491]: Order of the Service of the Holy Passion in the Patriarchal Church: Procession, Vesting, and Entourage (§ Appendix 5). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p863 (printed page 848) and facing English leaf p864 (printed page 849). Patriarchal ceremonial for the Twelve Passion Gospels (*Τῶν Ἁγίων Παθῶν*) on Holy and Great Thursday evening: Bells peal at the Twelfth Hour [6:00 p.m.]. His All-Holiness the Ecumenical Patriarch descends with his entourage half an hour later. The procession is led by four staff-bearing ushers (*κλητῆρες ῥαβδοῦχοι*) proclaiming the Patriarch's arrival, followed by all parish clergy and the Great Archimandrite, and the Great Ecclesiarch bearing the pastoral staff (*πατριαρχικὴ ποιμαντικὴ ῥάβδος* / *Pateritsa*). The Patriarch walks bearing a plain, unadorned walking staff (*χαζράνιον* / *Chazranion*), flanked by the Great Protosynkellos on his right and the Great Archdeacon on his left, followed by the junior deacons. At the Great Gate of the church, the Patriarch is vested with the Mandyas by the Great Archdeacon, and the pastoral staff is ceremonially transferred to him by the Protosynkellos. The procession enters the nave led by the Great Primikirios carrying the large double-branched candlestick (*διβάμβουλον* / *Divamvulon*). In the center of the nave, the Patriarch blesses the congregation while the Choirs sing "For many years, Master!" (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη, Δέσποτα*). [Printed Note: The *Chazranion* is a plain cane devoid of ornamentation, uniquely carried during the solemnity of Great and Holy Week].

[^492]: Order of the Service of the Holy Passion: Opening Rubrics, Hexapsalmos, and Troparion (§ Appendix 6). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p865 (printed page 850) and facing English leaf p866 (printed page 851). Sacerdotal action and introductory Matins order for the Twelve Gospels: The Patriarch ascends the Throne; the Great Archimandrite, Great Archdeacon, and Second Deacon receive Keron (*καιρόν*), followed by the junior deacons. The Great Archimandrite, vested in Epitrachilion at the Holy Table, intones the opening blessing: "Blessed is our God always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." (*Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and the Patriarch recites the Trisagion Prayers. The Reader-Priest reads the introductory Royal Psalms (Psalms 19 and 20 LXX), during which the Archimandrite, vested in Phelonion and preceded by a candle-bearer, censes the whole church using a hand censer (*Κατζί* / *Katzion*). Following the Trisagion exclamation and customary royal troparia, the Archimandrite intones the augmented petition and exclamation: "Glory to the holy, consubstantial, life-creating, and undivided Trinity, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.", whereupon the Patriarch recites the Six Psalms (*Ἑξάψαλμος*). After the Great Litany, the Choirs chant "Alleluia" four times with the appointed verses from Isaiah 26:9, 11, 15 (LXX), followed by the Troparion in Tone 8: "When the glorious disciples were enlightened at the washing of the feet..." (*Ὅτε οἱ ἔνδοξοι μαθηταί*), sung twice slowly and once moderately fast (*ἀργοσυντόμως*). During this hymn, the concelebrating Hierarchs exit the Sanctuary led by the Great Ecclesiarch to take their stations, and the Archdeacon enters the Bema to vest. [Editorial Note: Violakis accidentally transposed the third and fourth verses of the Alleluia in the Greek text].

[^493]: Order of the Service of the Holy Passion: Gospels 1 and 2, Antiphons, and Kathismata (§ Appendix 7). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p867 (printed page 852) and facing English leaf p868 (printed page 853). Proclamation of the Passion Gospels and hierarchical rotations: The vested Deacons exit the Royal Doors holding Dikerotrikera and flank the Patriarchal Throne. As "When the glorious disciples..." is sung for the third time, the Patriarch descends, enters the Sanctuary, vests with Epitrachilion and Omophorion, and the Holy Gospel is placed upon the Triskelion before the Royal Doors. Following the liturgical dialogue intoned by the Great Archdeacon, the Patriarch proclaims the First Passion Gospel (John 13:31–18:1). After blessing the faithful with the Trikirion, the Patriarch unvests in the Bema and returns to his Throne. The Choirs sing the 15 Antiphons of Holy Friday Matins. During the Second Antiphon, the Great Ecclesiarch invites the senior Hierarch, who receives Keron from the Patriarch, vests in the Bema, and upon the conclusion of the Kathisma in Tone 7 ("While feeding the disciples at the Supper..."), reads the Second Passion Gospel (John 18:1–28) at the Triskelion. At each Gospel reading, the Choirs alternate singing rapidly: "Glory to Thy forbearance, O Lord, glory to Thee!" (*Δόξα τῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σου, Κύριε, δόξα σοι*).

[^494]: Order of the Service of the Holy Passion: Gospels 3–6, Antiphons 4–15, and the Procession of the Crucified (§ Appendix 8). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p869 (printed page 854) and facing English leaf p870 (printed page 855). Succession of Gospel readings and the dramatic Solemn Procession of the Crucified Cross: Officiating Hierarchs read successive Gospels in order of seniority; remaining Gospels are proclaimed by the Great Protosynkellos, Grand Chancellor-Secretary (*Ἀρχιγραμματεύς*), Great Archimandrite, and Synkellos. After Gospel 2, Choir 2 sings Antiphons 4–6 and Kathisma in Tone 7 ("What manner of way, O Judas..."), followed by Gospel 3 (Matt. 26:57–75). Choir 1 sings Antiphons 7–9 and Kathisma in Tone 8 ("Oh, how did Judas..."), followed by Gospel 4 (John 18:28–19:16). Choir 2 sings Antiphons 10–12 and Kathisma in Tone 8 ("When Thou, O God, stoodest before Caiaphas..."), followed by Gospel 5 (Matt. 27:3–32). Choir 1 sings Antiphons 13–15 through the Theotokion ("Rejoice, thou who through the Angel..."). The Great Archimandrite, vested in Epitrachilion and Phelonion, lifts the Crucifix (*Ἐσταυρωμένος*), circumambulates the Holy Table, and intones in a sorrowful recitative the Idiomelon in Tone 6 [Tone 2 Plagal]: "Today He Who suspended the earth upon the waters is suspended upon the Tree!" (*Σήμερον κρεμᾶται ἐπὶ ξύλου*). Preceded by the Primikirios, candle-bearers, and censing Deacons, he carries the Cross into the center of the Nave and erects it in its floor socket. Choir 1 repeats the Idiomelon, and Choir 2 sings the concluding Stichera of Antiphon 15 and Kathisma in Tone 4 ("Thou hast redeemed us from the curse of the Law..."), leading into Gospel 6 (Mark 15:16–32) and the Beatitudes. [Printed Note 1: Historical note by George Violakis noting that the Procession of the Crucified was introduced into the Patriarchal Church under Ecumenical Patriarch Sophronios IV (1864) and had not existed in earlier printed Triodia or ancient Typika, but was sanctioned to meet the intense piety of the faithful].
